## Install and prepare the environment {#installation}

<div class="lesson-intro">Install and confirm the environment, then choose one progressive module. Reading the entire reference is not a prerequisite.</div>

### Install and inspect the environment {#installation-requirements}
R ≥4.1.0 and ggplot2 ≥4.0.0 are required. Installation and examples target v0.16.6.

```{r example-1, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("remotes", "dplyr", "purrr", "tidyr"))
remotes::install_github("DangJem/ggchord@v0.16.6")
library(ggchord)
packageVersion("ggchord")
```

#### Which version are you using? {#installation-source}
This tutorial documents **ggchord 0.16.6**. The installation above pins its formal tag; see [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/releases/tag/v0.16.6) for release assets.
For a source checkout, run from its repository root:

```{r example-2, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("pkgload")
pkgload::load_all(".")
packageVersion("ggchord")
```

Use the loading route appropriate to your source; you do not need both installation paths.
Record the version when reproducing a plot. This lesson needs neither optional Bioconductor packages nor Biopython.

#### Support evidence {#installation-support-evidence}
Declared lower bounds are R 4.1.0 and ggplot2 4.0.0. Release checks and actual platform versions are recorded in the release acceptance report; these do not certify every dependency combination. Optional readers require their documented dependencies.

### Choose a learning path {#installation-first-steps}
1. [Module I · Chord: learn the three tables](#chord-data), then import, backbones, layers and geometry.
2. [Module II · Collinear: reuse the chord inputs](#collinear-data), then switch coordinates, route links and focus locally.
3. [Module III · Plasmid: start with one sequence and DNA](#plasmid-data), then add layers and explore 13 reference cases.

Starting with chord follows ggchord's development order. See the [learning map](#articles). The two-sequence exercise below is an optional environment check rather than a substitute for the modules.

### Which columns come first? {#installation-input}
Sequences need accver/length; links need two IDs and four endpoints; genes need accver/start/end/strand. [Module I's first lesson](#chord-data) explains real tables, optional fields and BLAST naming.

### Optional: check one complete plot {#installation-first-plot}
Run the whole folded block, then inspect the figure. Bundled source-backed records need no external files or BLAST run.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-3, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
ids <- c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1")
first_sequences <- seq_data_example |>
  filter(accver %in% ids) |>
  select(accver, length)
first_genes <- gene_data_example |>
  filter(accver %in% ids) |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)
first_links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  filter(qaccver %in% ids, saccver %in% ids) |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)

first_colours <- setNames(c("#E64B35", "#233E4A"), ids)
p_first <- ggchord(
  seq_data = first_sequences, ribbon_data = first_links,
  gene_data = first_genes
) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#82B6AD", alpha = .55) +
  geom_seq(colour = "#233E4A", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_gene(aes(gene_fill = accver), position = position_strand(.10), width = .045) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  coord_collinear() +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(
    values = first_colours, name = "Sequence",
    guide = guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = theme(
      legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"), legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
      legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"), legend.margin = margin(l = 7, unit = "mm")
    ))
  ) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL) +
  theme_ggchord_publication(axis.text = element_text(size = 11)) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFCF5", colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  )
p_first
```

</details>

### Read the quick result {#installation-read}
Arrows retain biological strands; colours identify sequences only. Ribbons are existing comparison intervals, not new homology results. This small linear example makes positions easy to read; the full chord module starts with backbones.

### Optional: save the quick result {#installation-save}
Run this only after the block above has created p_first:


```{r example-4, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("first-comparison.png", p_first, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


Use the same 10×5 in dimensions for preview and export; see [output](#output).

For missing objects, run the preparation block. For missing functions, check the package version. getwd() determines the save directory. Optional readers need dependencies only in their own topics; basic modules do not require Bioconductor or Biopython.


## Choose your learning module {#modes}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Choose a layout for your question. The examples below compare three views using source-backed bundled records.</p></div>

### Which view should you choose? {#modes-choose}
| Task | Preferred view | Avoid this misreading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overall relationships among several sequences | Chord | Crossings alone are not evidence of inversion |
| Annotations on one plasmid or circular sequence | Circular | Multiple sequences do not fit a single-sequence coordinate |
| Positions, gene order and local neighbourhoods | Collinear | Display alignment or flipping is not a biological conclusion |

All three consume existing data; none computes a new BLAST alignment. Try the minimal combinations below, then follow the [raw-record workflow](#real-data), [complete plasmid map](#plasmids) or [local homolog comparison](#homology).

### Prepare this page {#modes-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-5, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
feature_palette <- c(
  CDS = "#993366", promoter = "#31849B", rep_origin = "#F1E51D",
  primer_bind = "#A020F0", misc_feature = "#A6ACB3", protein_bind = "#31849B"
)

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}

library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
features <- feature_source |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
```

### Chord: compare multiple sequences {#modes-chord}

```{r example-6, eval=FALSE}
p_chord <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = links, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = qaccver), alpha = .7) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_manual(values = seq_palette, guide = "none") +
  geom_seq(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(.1), width = .04) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4, seq_label_radius = .84, seq_label_hjust = .5) +
  coord_chord() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  doc_theme
p_chord
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/chord.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/chord.jpg" alt="Bundled sequences and alignment intervals in a chord view" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Bundled sequences and alignment intervals in a chord view · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Links are coloured by query sequence ID using the backbone category palette; this does not encode identity or homolog groups. See the [raw-record workflow](#real-data-chord) for colour mapped to reported identity.
`coord_chord()` controls global rotation and fitting. Sequence-local radius,
curvature, gap and orientation belong to `geom_seq()`. A NULL link control point
uses the historical origin-based chord route; it does not mean a universal
straight link. Ribbon avoidance defaults to `uniform`, line avoidance to `none`.

### Collinear: align local comparisons {#modes-collinear}

```{r example-7, eval=FALSE}
anchors <- genes |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  slice_max(end - start, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(accver, start, end)
p_collinear <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = links, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = qaccver), alpha = .7) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_manual(values = seq_palette, guide = "none") +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(.1)) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  coord_collinear(anchor = anchors, align = "center", orientation = "auto") +
  doc_axis() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  doc_theme
p_collinear
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/collinear.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/collinear.jpg" alt="Bundled records aligned to explicitly selected annotation anchors" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Bundled records aligned to explicitly selected annotation anchors · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
Each sequence is anchored to its own longest known gene for display; this does not assert homology.
`anchor` aligns specified intervals; `orientation = "auto"` chooses supported
orientations using available evidence. Inspect orientation diagnostics rather
than assuming biological inversion. Ribbons connect adjacent displayed rows by
default; use `adjacent_only = FALSE` or explicit `pairs` to retain others.
Non-adjacent outlines default to dashed; explicit styles take priority. These
rules differ from chord mode. [Focus and segments](#views) preserve source
coordinates for cropped or locally reversed views.

### Circular: annotate one sequence {#modes-circular}

```{r example-8, eval=FALSE}
circle_features <- features |>
  filter(type %in% c("CDS", "rep_origin"))
p_circular <- ggchord(seq_data = plasmid_seq) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_feature(aes(feature_fill = type), data = circle_features, position = position_plasmid()) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = circle_features, position = position_plasmid(), size = 4) +
  geom_seq_center_label() +
  scale_feature_fill_manual(values = feature_palette, breaks = unique(circle_features$type)) +
  coord_circular() +
  doc_theme
p_circular
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/circular.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/circular.jpg" alt="pUC19 annotations in a circular map" width="1296" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 annotations in a circular map · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
This example selects CDS and the replication origin for display, retaining the full sequence bp axis.
`coord_circular()` requires a single sequence. General features can carry unknown
strand. `geom_feature_plasmid()` is a convenience preset with its own defaults;
choose it explicitly when those defaults fit the task. Primer and restriction
layers are described in [recognition](#recognition).

### Check your result {#modes-check-result}
First count sequences: use circular for one annotated sequence, chord for the overall link pattern, and collinear for positions, distances or neighbourhoods.

## 1.1 Tables and field meanings {#chord-data}

Learn the tables before selecting layers. Chord comparison was ggchord's original core view. Its early BLAST workflows explain the compact field names retained today. A multi-sequence chord view displays existing interval comparisons among sequences; drawing does not run a multiple-sequence alignment algorithm.

### Minimal shapes of three tables {#chord-data-tables}
| Table | Required columns | One row represents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seq_data | accver, length | One sequence and its full length in bp |
| ribbon_data | qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send | One observed pair of aligned intervals |
| gene_data | accver, start, end, strand | One directed gene interval |

Backbones alone need neither links nor genes. Use `geom_feature()` for annotations with unknown strand rather than assigning a direction.

### Names and optional columns {#chord-data-names}
`accver` originated from accession.version, but any stable contig identifier is allowed; versions are not added or removed. `q` means query and `s` means subject. Both IDs must occur in the sequence table.

`pident` is percentage identity, needed only for identity mapping/filtering. Alignment `length` differs from full sequence `length`. Keep `evalue`, `bitscore`, `qlen` and `slen` when required by an analysis. Gene `anno` is optional annotation text; supply it for labels. Additional category columns can feed `aes()` without becoming mandatory inputs.

### Inspect real tables {#chord-data-inspect}
```{r example-9, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
seq_data_example |> select(accver, length) |> slice_head(n = 3)
ribbon_data_example |> select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send) |> slice_head(n = 3)
gene_data_example |> transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand, anno) |> slice_head(n = 3)
```

These are bundled source-backed records. This historical teaching fixture stores biological strand separately in `source_strand`; restore it explicitly. Newly read GFF3 annotations use their ordinary `strand` column.

### Coordinates and directions {#chord-data-coordinates}
Use one-based inclusive bp coordinates. Genes have ordered bounds with a separate strand. Endpoint order can represent reverse alignments; do not sort every link. Maximum feature endpoints do not establish full sequence lengths. See the [coordinate contract](#data-coordinates).

Continue to [1.2 From analysis results to input tables](#chord-import).


## 1.2 Produce and import comparisons {#chord-import}

Start with sequences and analysis results, then read them with ggchord. Missing comparisons must not be invented to populate a figure.

### Start with FASTA and GFF3 {#chord-import-files}
Extract the [tutorial bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) so the working directory contains `examples/`. FASTA supplies full lengths; GFF3 supplies intervals and strands. Retain source records separately from display tables.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-10, eval=FALSE}
# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),

  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

```

</details>

```{r example-11, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
# Original repository records; extract the tutorial input bundle first.
show_sequences <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna") |>
  select(accver, length)
show_annotations <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep")
show_genes <- show_annotations |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
show_alignments <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv")
# At most three substantial observed HSPs per pair; no coordinates are invented.
show_links <- show_alignments |>
  filter(length >= 900, pident >= 75) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Select up to four source CDS per sequence, spread across annotation order.
# No feature is moved or invented; keep complete source tables separately.
show_features <- show_genes |>
  filter(end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(display_bin = ntile(row_number(), 4), informative = !is.na(anno) & anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver, display_bin) |>
  arrange(desc(informative), desc(end - start), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
# Also retain well-separated negative-strand CDS, if not already represented.
show_reverse <- show_genes |>
  filter(strand == "-", end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(c(1, n())) |>
  ungroup()
show_features <- bind_rows(show_features, show_reverse) |>
  distinct(accver, start, end, strand, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(accver, start)
show_labels <- show_features
show_optimization <- optimize_ggchord_layout(
  show_sequences, show_links,
  optimize = "orientation", weight = "length"
)
```


`show_alignments` retains 32 observed HSPs and `show_links` selects 12. `show_genes` retains 266 CDS; `show_features` selects CDS of at least 500 bp from four groups across annotation order per sequence, additionally retaining source-backed negative-strand endpoints. Selection neither reruns alignment nor establishes functional homology.

For coordinate inspection, reshape the four endpoint columns with tidyr while retaining the original link table:


```{r example-12, eval=FALSE}
link_endpoints <- show_links |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(qstart, qend, sstart, send),
    names_to = c("side", "endpoint"), names_pattern = "([qs])(start|end)",
    values_to = "position"
  )
head(link_endpoints)
```


### Produce your own BLAST results {#chord-import-blast}
These producer commands are for analysts with BLAST installed and their own input files; the website builder does not execute them.

```sh
blastn -query query.fna -subject subject.fna -outfmt 6 -out result.tsv
```

```{r example-13, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
blast_source <- read_blast(file = "result.tsv")
```

Without a custom field list, outfmt 6 uses the standard 12-column table; 7 adds comments. Omitting outfmt entirely requests another format. Query/subject IDs map to qaccver/saccver. Consult the [NCBI field documentation](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK279684/table/appendices.T.options_common_to_all_blast/) and [nucleotide/protein guide](#alignments). Historical tutorial HSPs are converted records, not newly run BLAST results.

### When another format already exists {#chord-import-alternatives}
| Source | Entry point | Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing table | as_ggchord_seq/feature/link | Explicit role mapping; retain the original |
| BED, PAF | read_bed, read_paf | Convert zero-based half-open coordinates only once |
| GenBank | read_genbank | Biopython required; preserve record and segmented-location provenance |
| GRanges, Seqinfo | as_ggchord_feature, as_ggchord_seq | Full lengths from Seqinfo; unknown strand stays unknown |
| GInteractions | as_ggchord_link, as_ggchord_seq | First anchor is query; full length context is still required |

These adapters address the request in [issue #2](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/issues/2). Current code provides the entries; the historical discussion does not certify every current combination. Missing optional packages are explicitly skipped locally. See [format conversion](#formats-ranges) for runnable optional-object examples and limitations.

Continue to [1.3 Build from backbones](#chord-build).


## 1.3 Build the layers step by step {#chord-build}

Complete each small step before the flagship example. All four views reuse the same records, making the effect of each added layer visible.

### Prepare this page {#chord-build-prepare}
Extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) first.
<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-14, eval=FALSE}
# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}

library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
# Original repository records; extract the tutorial input bundle first.
show_sequences <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna") |>
  select(accver, length)
show_annotations <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep")
show_genes <- show_annotations |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
show_alignments <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv")
# At most three substantial observed HSPs per pair; no coordinates are invented.
show_links <- show_alignments |>
  filter(length >= 900, pident >= 75) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Select up to four source CDS per sequence, spread across annotation order.
# No feature is moved or invented; keep complete source tables separately.
show_features <- show_genes |>
  filter(end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(display_bin = ntile(row_number(), 4), informative = !is.na(anno) & anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver, display_bin) |>
  arrange(desc(informative), desc(end - start), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
# Also retain well-separated negative-strand CDS, if not already represented.
show_reverse <- show_genes |>
  filter(strand == "-", end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(c(1, n())) |>
  ungroup()
show_features <- bind_rows(show_features, show_reverse) |>
  distinct(accver, start, end, strand, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(accver, start)
show_labels <- show_features
show_optimization <- optimize_ggchord_layout(
  show_sequences, show_links,
  optimize = "orientation", weight = "length"
)
```

</details>

### Step 1: sequence backbones {#chord-build-backbones}

```{r example-15, eval=FALSE}
p_learn_seq <- ggchord(seq_data = show_sequences) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(
    values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
    guide = sequence_guide
  ) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20000, 40000), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  coord_chord() +
  doc_theme
p_learn_seq
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/learnseq.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/learnseq.jpg" alt="Chord step1: sequence backbones" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Chord step1: sequence backbones · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
`geom_seq()` draws backbones, `geom_seq_label()` identifies sequences, and `coord_chord()` selects the global view. No links or genes are required yet.

### Step 2: observed comparisons {#chord-build-links}

```{r example-16, eval=FALSE}
p_learn_links <- p_learn_seq +
  geom_link_ribbon(
    aes(ribbon_fill = pident),
    data = show_links,
    adjacent_only = FALSE, link_avoid = "smooth"
  ) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values, limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  )
p_learn_links
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/learnlinks.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/learnlinks.jpg" alt="Chord step2: observed comparisons" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Chord step2: observed comparisons · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
Identity belongs in aes and a scale. Explicitly retaining non-neighbour links keeps the same link data when replacing coordinates later.

### Step 3: selected genes {#chord-build-genes}

```{r example-17, eval=FALSE}
p_learn_genes <- p_learn_links +
  geom_gene(data = show_features, position = position_strand(0.08)) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand") +
  guides(gene_fill = strand_guide)
p_learn_genes
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/learngenes.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/learngenes.jpg" alt="Chord step3: selected genes" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Chord step3: selected genes · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
`position_strand()` separates positive and negative strands. Display selected real annotations while retaining every source CDS separately.

### Step 4: label every displayed feature {#chord-build-labels}

```{r example-18, eval=FALSE}
p_learn_labels <- p_learn_genes +
  geom_gene_label_repel(
    data = show_features, label_layout = "arc", label_wrap = 24,
    label_max_lines = 3, position = position_strand(0.08), size = 3
  )
p_learn_labels
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/learnlabels.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/learnlabels.jpg" alt="Chord step4: labels for selected features" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Chord step4: labels for selected features · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
The arrow and repel-label layers receive the same feature table without another label filter. Renaming, deleting or reordering records can change meaning; retain clear intermediate objects.

Continue to [1.4 Direction, radius, curvature and clearance](#chord-tuning).


## 1.4 Direction, curvature and clearance {#chord-tuning}

These controls have different owners: geoms configure sequence geometry, Positions place local features, coords select the global view, and scales/guides control encodings.

### Inspect directional evidence first {#chord-tuning-prepare}
Extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) first.

### Inspect directional evidence {#chord-tuning-orientation}
`show_optimization` optimizes display orientation only, preserving sequence order and weighting observed alignment lengths. Inspect seq_orientation and score_before/score_after. A display flip is not a new biological inversion result; the heuristic does not guarantee a global optimum.

### Combine capabilities into a readable view {#chord-tuning-parameters}

```{r example-20, eval=FALSE}
show_curvature <- c(
  "MT108731.1" = 0, "MT118296.1" = 0.85,
  "OQ646790.1" = 1.1, "OR222515.1" = -0.4
)
show_radius <- c(
  "MT108731.1" = 1, "MT118296.1" = 1.05,
  "OQ646790.1" = 0.95, "OR222515.1" = 1.08
)
p_show_chord <- ggchord(show_sequences, show_links, show_features) +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident), link_avoid = "smooth", alpha = 0.58, linewidth = 0.18) +
  geom_seq(
    seq_orientation = show_optimization$seq_orientation,
    seq_curvature = show_curvature, seq_radius = show_radius,
    seq_gap = 0.06, linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(0.07), width = 0.035) +
  geom_gene_label_repel(
    data = show_labels, label_layout = "radial", label_wrap = 24,
    size = 3.1, label_max_lines = 3, position = position_strand(0.07)
  ) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4, seq_label_radius = 0.84, seq_label_hjust = 0.5) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(
    values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
    guide = sequence_guide
  ) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand") +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  ) +
  guides(gene_fill = strand_guide) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20000, 40000), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  coord_chord(rotation = 50) +
  doc_theme +
  labs(
    title = "Four genomes, one connected view",
    subtitle = "Signed curvature and radius · selected strand-aware CDS · local ribbon clearance"
  )
p_show_chord
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/showcasechord.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/showcasechord.jpg" alt="Four-genome chord comparison with mixed backbone curvature and measured identity" width="1728" height="1440" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Four-genome chord comparison with mixed backbone curvature and measured identity · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
Named vectors match sequence IDs. Curvature 0 is straight, signed values bend in opposite directions, and magnitude changes bow depth. Radius changes sequence placement. The result combines automatic orientation, varying radius, zero/positive/negative curvature and local clearance without changing source coordinates.

### Why clearance modes look different {#chord-tuning-clearance}
`link_avoid = "uniform"` clears the whole endpoint interval. `"smooth"` retreats locally near feature polygons; `"none"` disables feature avoidance. Automatic clearance requires `link_gap = NULL`; a fixed number overrides it. Clearance considers feature geometry, not text, and does not automatically route around intervening sequence rows.

### Guides and export {#chord-tuning-guides}
Identity uses a long left-side colourbar; sequence and strand keys remain below. Explicit strand overrides mirror the arrow glyphs. See [styling](#styling) for guide responsibilities. Save at 12×10 in, then review [1.7 The complete showcase](#chord).


## 1.5 Filter and summarize links {#ribbons}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Reduce link clutter while retaining provenance: filtering, deduplication, merging and bundling have different meanings.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#ribbons-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed. For file-based examples, first extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) so the working directory contains `examples/`.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-21, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)

  select(accver, length)

  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),

)

identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)

strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)

  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",

library(dplyr)
sequence_source <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna", source_file = TRUE)
seq_real <- sequence_source |>
  select(accver, length)
annotation_source <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep", source_file = TRUE)
feature_real <- annotation_source |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
alignment_source <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv", source_file = TRUE)
link_real <- alignment_source |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send, pident, length)
real_validation <- validate_ggchord_data(seq_real, link_real)
real_validation

real_prepared <- prepare_ggchord_data(seq_real, link_real,
  features = list(annotation = feature_real)
)
real_filtered <- filter_ggchord_ribbons(link_real, min_pident = 80, min_length = 500)
# Explicit display subset: the six longest CDS per sequence; raw annotations stay intact.
real_display_features <- feature_real |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  slice_max(end - start + 1, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
real_labels <- real_display_features |>
  filter(anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  slice_head(n = 2) |>
  ungroup()
real_filtered$report
```

</details>

### Begin with the original link table {#ribbons-input}
Use the [real-record workflow](#real-data-selection) to create `seq_real`,
`link_real` and `real_filtered`. Keep its original tables and filter report.


```{r example-22, eval=FALSE}
unique_links <- deduplicate_ggchord_ribbons(real_filtered$data,
  by = "overlap",
  min_reciprocal_overlap = .9
)
merged_links <- merge_ggchord_ribbons(unique_links$data,
  max_gap = 100,
  min_pident_difference = 2
)
bundled_links <- bundle_ggchord_ribbons(link_real, seq_real, bins = 30)
p_density <- ggchord(seq_real, link_real, validate = "none") +
  geom_seq(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4, seq_label_radius = .84, seq_label_hjust = .5) +
  stat_ribbon_density(aes(ribbon_alpha = after_stat(density)), fill = "#269B82") +
  scale_ribbon_alpha_continuous(
    name = "Relative density", range = c(.1, .6),
    guide = guide_ggchord_legend(position = "bottom", nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
  ) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  coord_chord() +
  doc_theme
p_bundle <- ggchord(seq_real, link_real, validate = "none") +
  geom_seq() +
  stat_ribbon_bundle(bins = 30, fill = "#269B82") +
  coord_chord() +
  doc_theme
p_density
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Filtered HSPs | 8 |
| After overlap deduplication | 8 |
| Merged display intervals | 8 |
| Bundle output rows | 28 |

### Understand each transformation {#ribbons-transformations}
Filtering keeps observations meeting declared thresholds. Reciprocal-overlap
deduplication selects a representative existing observation; it does not sum
identities. Merging combines nearby compatible intervals into a display envelope.
Bundling groups nearby query/subject locations into an aggregate. Inspect each
`$report` and source-row membership, especially when extra metadata conflict.
The merged or bundled envelope is not a newly computed nucleotide alignment.
Estimated lengths retain their flags; unobserved identity is never invented.

### Density is an explicit statistic {#ribbons-density}
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/density.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/density.jpg" alt="Interval density from the original alignment observations" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Interval density from the original alignment observations · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

`stat_ribbon_density()` maps a computed density, and `stat_ribbon_bundle()` performs
its explicit aggregation during build. The ordinary ribbon geom still draws one
ribbon per row. Interpret count, reported length and identity weighting in their
own units; more opaque ribbons need not mean stronger independently validated
homology. A point anchor without direction evidence cannot acquire an aggregate
orientation merely because its endpoints are equal.

### Choose interval ribbons or point links {#ribbons-points}
After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-23, eval=FALSE}
# Midpoints summarize existing HSPs for display; they are not new alignments.
points <- ribbon_data_example |>
  transmute(
    qaccver, saccver,
    qpos = floor((qstart + qend) / 2),
    spos = floor((sstart + send) / 2),
    pident
  )
p_points <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  geom_link_line(aes(link_colour = pident),
    data = points,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(2, "mm")), linewidth = .7
  ) +
  scale_link_colour_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks,
    name = "Identity (%)", guide = guide_ggchord_colourbar(
      available_aes = "link_colour",
      position = "bottom", direction = "horizontal",
      theme = doc_legend_theme + theme(legend.key.width = unit(65, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"))
    )
  ) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  coord_chord() +
  doc_theme
p_points
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/pointlinks.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/pointlinks.jpg" alt="Midpoint links derived from existing HSP intervals" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Midpoint links derived from existing HSP intervals · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Point positions are integer midpoints of real bundled HSPs; identity remains the reported `pident`. Lines use `qpos/spos`,
not interval ends, and an arrow points from query to subject. The line default
avoidance is `none`; ribbon avoidance is `uniform`. Global chord rotation belongs
to the coordinate system. Pair selection and adjacent-row defaults in linear
plots are covered in [three modes](#modes-collinear).

The point-link colour scale supplies `available_aes = "link_colour"` to its
colourbar explicitly. Ordinary ggplot2 colourbars and the wrapper default do not
accept every extended role; choose the matching role when making a custom guide.

### Check your result {#ribbons-check-result}
Inspect each report and member rows before reading the plot. Aggregated bands are not new alignments; point links summarize midpoints of existing HSPs.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#views">Focus, segments and homology →</a></div>


## 1.6 Full source-file workflow {#real-data}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Combine original FASTA, GFF3 and standard BLAST tables into a traceable comparison. Inspect inputs, choose a display subset, then compare chord and full-length views.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#real-data-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed. For file-based examples, first extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) so the working directory contains `examples/`.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-24, eval=FALSE}
# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}
```

</details>

This complete workflow uses four sequence records already present in the source
repository. It requires the matching development checkout or the tutorial input
bundle, not new alignments or external gene prediction. [Download the inputs](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples)
and unpack them so `examples/` is under the working directory. Record the package
version and [build manifest](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/website) with the exported figure.

### 1. Read and inspect original records {#real-data-read}

```{r example-25, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
sequence_source <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna", source_file = TRUE)
seq_real <- sequence_source |>
  select(accver, length)
annotation_source <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep", source_file = TRUE)
feature_real <- annotation_source |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
alignment_source <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv", source_file = TRUE)
link_real <- alignment_source |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send, pident, length)
real_validation <- validate_ggchord_data(seq_real, link_real)
real_validation
```


The FASTA headers supply exact accession versions and lengths. GFF3 contributes
CDS intervals and their original strands. BLAST output contributes existing
alignments; the reader does not run BLAST. Inspect `real_validation` before
continuing: decreasing link endpoints can be legitimate reverse-direction hits.
Never turn unknown annotation strands into `+` to make a gene shortcut accept them.

### 2. Make the display selection explicit {#real-data-selection}

```{r example-26, eval=FALSE}
real_prepared <- prepare_ggchord_data(seq_real, link_real,
  features = list(annotation = feature_real)
)
real_filtered <- filter_ggchord_ribbons(link_real, min_pident = 80, min_length = 500)
# Explicit display subset: the six longest CDS per sequence; raw annotations stay intact.
real_display_features <- feature_real |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  slice_max(end - start + 1, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
real_labels <- real_display_features |>
  filter(anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  slice_head(n = 2) |>
  ungroup()
real_filtered$report
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Sequences | 4 |
| Annotation rows | 266 |
| CDS selected for the chord view | 24 |
| Original HSPs | 32 |
| HSPs retained by the display filter | 8 |
| Selected text labels | 6 |

The link display retains identity ≥80% and reported alignment length ≥500 bp.
The chord view selects the six longest imported CDS per sequence, labelling at most two selected CDS with informative annotations (excluding
hypothetical protein). These are display rules, not biological findings or a claim
that omitted genes are absent. Raw `feature_real` and `link_real` remain intact;
`real_prepared$report` and `real_filtered$report` retain preparation/filter evidence.
No display strands are recoded. This differs from the small packaged teaching
fixture whose documented generation includes display-strand recoding.

### 3. Build a chord comparison {#real-data-chord}

```{r example-27, eval=FALSE}
p_real_chord <- ggchord(seq_data = seq_real, ribbon_data = real_filtered$data, validate = "none") +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident), alpha = .65) +
  geom_seq(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_feature(aes(feature_fill = strand),
    data = real_display_features,
    width = .045, position = position_strand(.08)
  ) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(
    data = real_labels, label_layout = "radial",
    label_wrap = 20, size = 4, position = position_strand(.08)
  ) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4, seq_label_radius = .84, seq_label_hjust = .5) +
  coord_chord() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_feature_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-")) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  ) +
  doc_theme
p_real_chord
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/realchord.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/realchord.jpg" alt="Original sequences with explicitly selected CDS and alignment links" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Original sequences with explicitly selected CDS and alignment links · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Read sequence labels first, then source-strand feature arrows and interval links.
Ribbons encode existing aligned intervals and mapped identity; their crossing is
not itself evidence of a rearrangement. The selected features remain visibly
separate from the much wider alignment spans. Use the full input tables when
scientific interpretation needs annotations outside this display subset.

### 4. Inspect all annotations in a linear view {#real-data-linear}

```{r example-28, eval=FALSE}
p_real_linear <- ggchord(seq_real, real_filtered$data, validate = "none") +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#6BAFA6", alpha = .45) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  geom_feature(data = feature_real, feature_fill = "#CE1536", show.legend = FALSE, position = position_strand(.18)) +
  geom_seq_scale(length = 10000) +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  doc_theme
p_real_linear
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/reallinear.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/reallinear.jpg" alt="Original sequences, all imported CDS and filtered links" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Original sequences, all imported CDS and filtered links · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

This view draws all imported annotations. Ribbons connect adjacent displayed
sequences by default; retaining every comparison is an explicit layer decision.
The bp scale bar belongs to collinear coordinates. See [local views](#views)
for cropping, source-coordinate axes and independent windows, and
[output](#output) to preview and save at the gallery's stated dimensions.

### 5. Keep the evidence with the figure {#real-data-provenance}
The input archive contains unmodified FASTA/GFF3/BLAST files, a SHA256 manifest
and the shared example script. The plot manifest records the code hash, PNG device,
width, height and dpi. The accession names identify source records; a drawing is
not a replacement for the original annotations or alignment evidence.

### Select fields before passing data {#real-data-minimal-fields}
The `*_source` objects keep original fields and provenance; `seq_real` has two
columns, `feature_real` only geometry/type/text, and `link_real` adds identity and
reported length only because this workflow filters and colours by them. Standard
12-column BLAST conversions are used, not a requirement for the historical 17 fields.
The bundled gene fixture preserves its original strand in `source_strand`; the
short examples restore that biological strand before selecting four gene columns.
See [alignment input](#alignments) for exact format and unit boundaries.

### Check your result {#real-data-check-result}
Check that IDs agree across the tables, inspect filtering reports and verify that guides encode identity and strand. Use the overview to locate regions, then focus a neighbourhood to study a CDS.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#homology">Explicit homologs and coding-coordinate links →</a></div>

### Save this result {#real-data-save-result}
Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

```{r example-29, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("phage-comparison.png", p_real_chord, width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## 1.7 Complete chord showcase {#chord}

<div class="lesson-intro">Bring four genomes into one connected view. Combine straight and curved backbones, strand-aware genes and a continuous identity scale without hiding where the data came from.</div>

### What this view shows {#chord-overview}
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/showcasechord.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/showcasechord.jpg" alt="Four-genome chord comparison with mixed backbone curvature and measured identity" width="1728" height="1440" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Four-genome chord comparison with mixed backbone curvature and measured identity · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

This is the end of Module I. Begin with [tables](#chord-data), [import](#chord-import), [layer construction](#chord-build) and [geometry/clearance](#chord-tuning). 18 selected real CDS each receive repel labels; the complete 266-row annotation source remains separate. The four backbones combine zero, positive and negative curvature, varying radii and optimized display directions.

### Prepare original records {#chord-prepare}
Extract the [tutorial input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) into the working directory, so it contains `examples/`. Install the optional example packages with `install.packages(c("dplyr", "purrr", "tidyr"))`; they prepare tables, map lists and inspect endpoint columns.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-30, eval=FALSE}
# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
```

</details>

```{r example-31, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
# Original repository records; extract the tutorial input bundle first.
show_sequences <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna") |>
  select(accver, length)
show_annotations <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep")
show_genes <- show_annotations |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
show_alignments <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv")
# At most three substantial observed HSPs per pair; no coordinates are invented.
show_links <- show_alignments |>
  filter(length >= 900, pident >= 75) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Select up to four source CDS per sequence, spread across annotation order.
# No feature is moved or invented; keep complete source tables separately.
show_features <- show_genes |>
  filter(end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(display_bin = ntile(row_number(), 4), informative = !is.na(anno) & anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver, display_bin) |>
  arrange(desc(informative), desc(end - start), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
# Also retain well-separated negative-strand CDS, if not already represented.
show_reverse <- show_genes |>
  filter(strand == "-", end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(c(1, n())) |>
  ungroup()
show_features <- bind_rows(show_features, show_reverse) |>
  distinct(accver, start, end, strand, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(accver, start)
show_labels <- show_features
show_optimization <- optimize_ggchord_layout(
  show_sequences, show_links,
  optimize = "orientation", weight = "length"
)
```


The input contains four unchanged FASTA records, their GFF3 annotations and 32 original HSPs. The display keeps HSPs at least 900 bp long and at least 75% identical, with at most three per sequence pair. This reduces clutter without merging or inventing alignments.

### Compose the layers {#chord-compose}

```{r example-32, eval=FALSE}
show_curvature <- c(
  "MT108731.1" = 0, "MT118296.1" = 0.85,
  "OQ646790.1" = 1.1, "OR222515.1" = -0.4
)
show_radius <- c(
  "MT108731.1" = 1, "MT118296.1" = 1.05,
  "OQ646790.1" = 0.95, "OR222515.1" = 1.08
)
p_show_chord <- ggchord(show_sequences, show_links, show_features) +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident), link_avoid = "smooth", alpha = 0.58, linewidth = 0.18) +
  geom_seq(
    seq_orientation = show_optimization$seq_orientation,
    seq_curvature = show_curvature, seq_radius = show_radius,
    seq_gap = 0.06, linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(0.07), width = 0.035) +
  geom_gene_label_repel(
    data = show_labels, label_layout = "radial", label_wrap = 24,
    size = 3.1, label_max_lines = 3, position = position_strand(0.07)
  ) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4, seq_label_radius = 0.84, seq_label_hjust = 0.5) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(
    values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
    guide = sequence_guide
  ) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand") +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  ) +
  guides(gene_fill = strand_guide) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20000, 40000), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  coord_chord(rotation = 50) +
  doc_theme +
  labs(
    title = "Four genomes, one connected view",
    subtitle = "Signed curvature and radius · selected strand-aware CDS · local ribbon clearance"
  )
p_show_chord
```


`geom_seq(seq_curvature = ...)` applies named values to stable sequence identifiers. `0` is a straight backbone. Curvature changes the display geometry; it does not alter sequence lengths, biological strands or alignment endpoints.

### Read and adapt the result {#chord-read}
Start with the sequence colours and gene directions, then trace the larger aligned intervals. A ribbon crossing is not evidence of a rearrangement by itself. The colour bar uses the same identity scale as the [collinear view](#collinear).

Use [link filtering](#ribbons) to change the display threshold, [labels](#labels) to choose annotation density, or [sequence parameters](#parameters) to change radius and curvature. For a file-by-file introduction, start with [original sequence comparisons](#real-data).

### Save at its intended size {#chord-save}
```{r example-33, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("four-genome-chord.png", p_show_chord, width = 12, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## 2.1 Reuse chord input tables {#collinear-data}

Collinearity extends ggchord's original chord grammar into a linear view. The design goal is to retain shared data and layers, switching coordinates wherever the contracts permit.

### The same three tables {#collinear-data-tables}
| Input | Required columns | Linear interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| seq_data | accver, length | One sequence per row with a shared bp x scale |
| ribbon_data | qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send | An observed interval correspondence between rows |
| gene_data | accver, start, end, strand | Genes separated above/below rows by a Position |

Optional fields and the historical BLAST naming follow [1.1](#chord-data). Identity needs pident; labels need anno. Source fields preserve coordinates in local windows; display gaps do not represent invented DNA lengths.

### Obtain the inputs {#collinear-data-import}
Reuse the FASTA/GFF3/BLAST workflow in [1.2](#chord-import), or import PAF, GRanges and GInteractions through [adapters](#formats). Protein alignments require [explicit CDS projection](#projection); aa endpoints must not be presented as bp.

### Current conversion boundaries {#collinear-data-contract}
The [next page](#collinear-build) demonstrates replacing coord alone. Explicit circular radius, curvature, ring and radial sequence-label placement are rejected by the current linear contract rather than silently ignored. Keep coordinate-specific styling in the appropriate showcase. Perfect conversion of every possible composition remains a design goal, not a current guarantee.

Linear views default to adjacent displayed rows. Set `adjacent_only = FALSE` in shared layers to retain the chord link set. Choose manual sequence directions or coordinate-owned automatic orientation, not both at once.


## 2.2 Switch coordinates and add layers {#collinear-build}

Verify the shared grammar before tuning linear composition. These objects replace only the coordinates on the chord teaching objects: no table edits or new alignments.

### Prepare this page {#collinear-build-prepare}
Extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) first.
<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-34, eval=FALSE}
# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}

library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
# Original repository records; extract the tutorial input bundle first.
show_sequences <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna") |>
  select(accver, length)
show_annotations <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep")
show_genes <- show_annotations |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
show_alignments <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv")
# At most three substantial observed HSPs per pair; no coordinates are invented.
show_links <- show_alignments |>
  filter(length >= 900, pident >= 75) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Select up to four source CDS per sequence, spread across annotation order.
# No feature is moved or invented; keep complete source tables separately.
show_features <- show_genes |>
  filter(end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(display_bin = ntile(row_number(), 4), informative = !is.na(anno) & anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver, display_bin) |>
  arrange(desc(informative), desc(end - start), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
# Also retain well-separated negative-strand CDS, if not already represented.
show_reverse <- show_genes |>
  filter(strand == "-", end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(c(1, n())) |>
  ungroup()
show_features <- bind_rows(show_features, show_reverse) |>
  distinct(accver, start, end, strand, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(accver, start)
show_labels <- show_features
show_optimization <- optimize_ggchord_layout(
  show_sequences, show_links,
  optimize = "orientation", weight = "length"
)
```

</details>
<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-35, eval=FALSE}
p_learn_seq <- ggchord(seq_data = show_sequences) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(
    values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
    guide = sequence_guide
  ) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20000, 40000), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  coord_chord() +
  doc_theme
p_learn_seq

p_learn_links <- p_learn_seq +
  geom_link_ribbon(
    aes(ribbon_fill = pident),
    data = show_links,
    adjacent_only = FALSE, link_avoid = "smooth"
  ) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values, limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  )
p_learn_links

p_learn_genes <- p_learn_links +
  geom_gene(data = show_features, position = position_strand(0.08)) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand") +
  guides(gene_fill = strand_guide)
p_learn_genes

p_learn_labels <- p_learn_genes +
  geom_gene_label_repel(
    data = show_features, label_layout = "arc", label_wrap = 24,
    label_max_lines = 3, position = position_strand(0.08), size = 3
  )
p_learn_labels
```

</details>

### Replace coord {#collinear-build-switch}

```{r example-36, eval=FALSE}
# Reuse exactly the same data and layers; replace only the coordinate system.
p_linear_seq <- p_learn_seq + coord_collinear()
p_linear_links <- p_learn_links + coord_collinear()
p_linear_labels <- p_learn_labels + coord_collinear(ratio = 0.65)
p_linear_labels
```

## 2.3 Routes, clearance and the ruler {#collinear-routing}

Adjacent and cross-row links impose different reading costs. Separate their data and controls while preserving observed HSP endpoints. Control points change display paths only.

Extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) first.
