### Specify controls for long links {#collinear-routing-routes}

```{r example-38, eval=FALSE}
# Omit two short, crowded candidates from this linear display only.
# Both source rows remain in show_features and in the chord display.
show_linear_features <- show_features |>
  filter(!anno %in% c("tail assembly protein", "gp4 protein"))
# Separate adjacent and cross-row links, retaining original endpoint values.
show_pair_rows <- show_links |>
  mutate(
    query_row = match(qaccver, show_sequences$accver),
    subject_row = match(saccver, show_sequences$accver),
    span = abs(query_row - subject_row)
  )
show_adjacent <- show_pair_rows |> filter(span == 1)
# One longest observed HSP per non-neighbour pair keeps the long routes legible.
show_cross <- show_pair_rows |>
  filter(span > 1) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Inspect a backbone-only layout using the same alignment and gap as the final view.
show_linear_coord <- coord_collinear(align = "center", orientation = "auto", ratio = 0.7)
show_routing_base <- ggchord(show_sequences, show_links) +
  geom_seq(seq_gap = 0.42) + show_linear_coord
show_reference <- get_chord_layout(show_routing_base)$sequence_reference
# Shared controls sit just beyond the intervening backbones, rather than far away.
show_cross_controls <- map2(show_cross$query_row, show_cross$subject_row, function(query_row, subject_row) {
  between <- seq(min(query_row, subject_row) + 1L, max(query_row, subject_row) - 1L)
  middle_ids <- show_sequences$accver[between]
  right_edge <- max(show_reference$x_offset[middle_ids] + show_reference$lens[middle_ids] * show_reference$x_scale)
  middle_y <- mean(show_reference$y[show_sequences$accver[c(query_row, subject_row)]])
  c(right_edge + if (abs(query_row - subject_row) == 3) 0.85 else 0.65, middle_y)
})
p_show_collinear <- ggchord(show_sequences, gene_data = show_linear_features) +
  geom_link_ribbon(
    aes(ribbon_fill = pident),
    data = show_adjacent,
    link_avoid = "smooth", alpha = 0.48, linewidth = 0.22
  ) +
  geom_link_ribbon(
    aes(ribbon_fill = pident),
    data = show_cross,
    adjacent_only = FALSE, link_ctrl_point = show_cross_controls,
    link_avoid = "smooth", alpha = 0.28, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_seq(seq_gap = 0.42, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(0.09), width = 0.045) +
  geom_gene_label_repel(
    data = show_linear_features |> arrange(desc(nchar(anno)), accver, start),
    label_layout = "auto", label_wrap = 24,
    label_side = "auto", position = position_strand(0.09), size = 3.3
  ) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  geom_seq_scale(length = 10000, offset = unit(c(0, 10), "mm")) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(
    values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
    guide = sequence_guide
  ) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand") +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  ) +
  guides(gene_fill = strand_guide) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20000, 40000, 60000, 80000), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  show_linear_coord +
  doc_theme +
  labs(
    title = "Sequence architecture, across four genomes",
    subtitle = "Selected labelled CDS · strand-separated arrows · routed cross-row comparisons"
  )
p_show_collinear
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/showcasecollinear.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/showcasecollinear.jpg" alt="Four-genome collinearity: strand-separated features and routed cross-row links" width="1728" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Four-genome collinearity: strand-separated features and routed cross-row links · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
The linear showcase omits the crowded tail assembly protein and gp4 protein candidates, retaining them in the source and chord view; the remaining 16 features are individually labelled. Keep the selected adjacent HSPs and one longest HSP per non-neighbour pair. `show_cross_controls` matches `show_cross` row order; rebuild both after sorting/filtering. Controls use exported layout x/y units, not bp. Each link accepts two or four numbers, shaping its two ribbon edges rather than invoking a global route planner.

Shorter sequences are horizontally centred. A backbone-only layout provides actual row positions, lengths and offsets; controls are placed just beyond the intervening right ends rather than far from the data. Row spacing uses seq_gap and the longest backbone width, while controls do not accept bp coordinates. Changing spacing, order or orientation requires inspecting the paths again; arbitrary controls are not guaranteed free of self-intersection.

### Local clearance and dashed outlines {#collinear-routing-clearance}
`position_strand()` separates strands. `link_avoid = "smooth"` with the default NULL gap retreats locally near arrows. Non-adjacent outlines are dashed by default; a larger linewidth makes them visible without overriding linetype. Adjacency follows display order, not biological alignment direction.

### Why the ruler was offset {#collinear-routing-ruler}
`geom_seq_scale()` defaults to a 2 mm horizontal and 6 mm vertical offset. The earlier inset was configuration, not incorrect bp conversion. `offset = unit(c(0, 10), "mm")` aligns the start with the left sequence envelope and reserves vertical label space. With centred rows, source coordinate0 is no longer aligned across sequences; the ruler uses the left envelope, and reversed rows have their source origin at the other end. A scale bar measures distance rather than a particular source interval.

### Continue in depth {#collinear-routing-next}
Use [focus/segments](#views) for local questions and [CDS neighbourhoods](#homology) for homology evidence; review the [2.6 Showcase](#collinear). GC remains available in [tracks](#tracks), while the flagship reserves space for labels and links.


## 2.4 Compare CDS neighbourhoods {#homology}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Compare AmpR neighbourhoods in two plasmids. Check real coding DNA, establish correspondence, then focus to each CDS plus 200 bp on either side.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#homology-prepare}
Only bundled data is needed; no download or new alignment. Load the package and optional display settings first.

### 1. Extract actual CDS and coding DNA {#homology-membership}
Select AmpR annotations from bundled pUC19 and pETDuet-1, retaining IDs, coordinates, strand and text. Reverse-complement negative-strand DNA so comparisons use the same biological orientation rather than annotation names alone.


```{r example-40, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
data(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_source <- bind_rows(plasmid_example_pUC19, plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_seq <- homolog_source |>
  select(accver, length)
cluster_features <- homolog_source |>
  find_common_features() |>
  filter(type == "CDS", anno == "AmpR") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno) |>
  arrange(match(accver, homolog_source$accver)) |>
  mutate(feature_id = paste(accver, start, end, sep = ":"))
# Membership is computed from exact strand-corrected CDS DNA equality, not gene names.
reverse_complement <- function(sequence) {
  bases <- strsplit(sequence, "")[[1]]
  chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", paste(rev(bases), collapse = ""))
}
coding_sequences <- cluster_features |>
  left_join(select(homolog_source, accver, sequence), by = "accver") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    coding_dna = substr(sequence, start, end),
    coding_dna = if (strand == "-") reverse_complement(coding_dna) else coding_dna
  ) |>
  ungroup()
cds_dna <- pull(coding_sequences, coding_dna)
```


`cluster_features` should contain two actual CDS; `cds_dna` retains their oriented coding sequences. This strict example checks exact DNA equality. General homology analysis can use external alignments and clustering; homologs need not be identical.

### 2. Declare members and sequence pairs {#homology-links}
Build membership from exact coding-DNA equality. Different DNA does not enter one group merely because both annotations say AmpR.


```{r example-41, eval=FALSE}
membership <- tibble(
  feature_id = cluster_features$feature_id,
  cluster_id = paste0("exact_CDS_", match(cds_dna, unique(cds_dna)))
)
homologs <- link_ggchord_clusters(cluster_features, membership,
  pairs = tibble(qaccver = homolog_seq$accver[1], saccver = homolog_seq$accver[2])
)
loci <- find_ggchord_loci(homolog_seq, cluster_features,
  targets = cluster_features$feature_id[cluster_features$anno == "AmpR"][1], upstream = 100, downstream = 100
)
```


Inspect `membership` and `homologs$report$comparisons` and `$members`. The linking utility consumes existing groups; it does not compute a new alignment. Unknown members and ambiguous paralogs are reported; only explicit `paralogs = "all"` requests all combinations within the documented bounds.

### 3. Focus on comparable neighbourhoods {#homology-focus}
Full plasmid lengths would shrink the individual CDS. Construct windows from each real CDS source interval and add 200 bp on either side, retaining the original sequence and annotation tables.


```{r example-42, eval=FALSE}
# Compare equivalent local windows instead of shrinking one gene on full plasmids.
homolog_windows <- cluster_features |>
  select(accver, start, end)
local_homologs <- focus_ggchord_data(homolog_seq, homologs$data, cluster_features,
  loci = homolog_windows, expand = 200
)
p_homologs <- ggchord(
  seq_data = local_homologs$seq_data,
  ribbon_data = local_homologs$ribbon_data, gene_data = local_homologs$gene_data
) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#269B82", alpha = .65) +
  geom_seq(colour = "#233E4A", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_feature(
    data = local_homologs$gene_data, feature_fill = "#F1D334",
    position = position_strand(.10), width = .07
  ) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = local_homologs$gene_data, size = 4, label_fit = "shrink") +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  geom_seq_break() +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis("source") +
  doc_theme
p_homologs
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/homologs.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/homologs.jpg" alt="AmpR neighbourhoods: identical CDS, 200 bp flanks and source coordinates" width="1440" height="720" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>AmpR neighbourhoods: identical CDS, 200 bp flanks and source coordinates · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Gold arrows identify the checked identical coding sequences; the purple band connects their CDS ranges and internal text names AmpR. Axes use each original sequence's positions, so one horizontal location can have different source labels. Break markers indicate that only local windows remain.

`local_homologs$report` records retention and clipping. Genes outside the windows are omitted, not absent. The band represents declared interval correspondence, not a base alignment; envelopes of segmented annotations likewise do not establish exon-level correspondence.

### 4. Project supported protein intervals to both CDS {#homology-projection}

```{r example-43, eval=FALSE}
# Exact CDS DNA equality supplies evidence for these selected ungapped residues.
matching <- homologs$data |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
paired_coding <- cluster_features |>
  mutate(phase = 0)
paired_cds <- build_ggchord_cds(paired_coding)
protein_link <- tibble(
  qfeature_id = matching$qfeature_id, sfeature_id = matching$sfeature_id,
  qstart = 1, qend = 20, sstart = 1, send = 20
)
projected_links <- project_ggchord_links(protein_link, paired_cds, ungapped = TRUE)
projected_links
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Projected genomic feature rows | 1 |
| Projected nucleotide link rows | 1 |

The first 20 residues of identical CDS provide sequence evidence for `ungapped = TRUE`. Equal spans alone do not justify that claim for ordinary BLASTp HSPs. The utility retains protein statistics rather than presenting them as nucleotide identity.

### Check your result {#homology-check-result}
Both internal labels should read AmpR and arrows retain the actual negative strand. Coding DNA supports correspondence; source axes and focus reports explain the local display. Save at [explicit 10 × 5 in dimensions](#output).

Next: [read real BLASTp query intervals](#alignments-protein), understand [CDS projection and segments](#projection), or create [independent local windows](#views).

### Save this result {#homology-save-result}
Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

```{r example-44, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("ampR-neighbourhood.png", p_homologs, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## 2.5 Focus, anchors and segments {#views}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Select local windows or segments while keeping source positions distinct from display transformations.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#views-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-45, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}
```

</details>

### Focus without losing origins {#views-focus}
After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-46, eval=FALSE}
focus_loci <- tibble(
  accver = seqs$accver,
  start = floor(seqs$length * .25), end = floor(seqs$length * .75)
)
focused <- focus_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes, loci = focus_loci)
p_focus <- ggchord(
  seq_data = focused$seq_data, ribbon_data = focused$ribbon_data,
  gene_data = focused$gene_data
) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#6BAFA6", alpha = .5) +
  geom_gene() +
  geom_seq_break() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  doc_axis("source") +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_theme
p_focus
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/focus.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/focus.jpg" alt="Focused sequence windows with source-coordinate axes" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Focused sequence windows with source-coordinate axes · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Focus relocates retained positions to local one-based coordinates and retains
source origins, truncation flags and a report. `boundary = "trim"` can clip
links by a linear display projection; it does not realign sequences. A scaled
alignment length is flagged as estimated. `coordinates = "source"` restores
source axis labels, including after repeated focusing.

### Independent windows and local reversal {#views-segments}

```{r example-47, eval=FALSE}
windows <- tibble(
  accver = rep(seqs$accver[1], 2),
  start = c(1, floor(seqs$length[1] * .65)), end = c(floor(seqs$length[1] * .4), seqs$length[1]),
  locus_id = c("left_window", "right_window"), row_id = seqs$accver[1], orientation = c(1, -1)
)
segmented <- segment_ggchord_data(slice_head(seqs, n = 1), windows = windows)
p_segments <- ggchord(seq_data = segmented$seq_data) +
  geom_seq() +
  coord_collinear(segments = segmented$segments, segment_gap = 2000)
p_segments
```


Each window has a reversible source mapping; omitted gaps have no mapping.
`map_ggchord_position()` maps explicit source positions into a plot for ordinary
ggplot2 annotations. Supply the window ID when windows share a source sequence.
Do not interpret display orientation as a change to the original strand.

### Explicit biological relationships {#views-homology}
`find_ggchord_loci()` selects declared feature/name queries. `link_ggchord_clusters()`
requires an explicit membership table and sequence pairs; equal gene names do
not establish homology. `filter_ggchord_ribbons()`, `deduplicate_ggchord_ribbons()`
and `merge_ggchord_ribbons()` prepare existing alignments, preserving source
membership and estimated-length flags. Bundle and density statistics summarize
provided links rather than creating new sequence alignments.

### Map an annotation back to source coordinates {#views-mapping}

```{r example-48, eval=FALSE}
source_position <- focus_loci$start[1] + 100
source_mark <- map_ggchord_position(p_focus, seqs$accver[1], source_position, source = TRUE)
p_marked <- p_focus +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = source_mark, aes(x, y),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#D59B17", size = 3
  )
p_marked
```


Run the [focus example](#views-focus) first. The helper returns Cartesian x/y
for a source position 100 bp inside the first selected window. It does not make all ordinary ggplot2 coordinates
become genomic bp. In segmented views choose the window ID, and check positions
in omitted gaps rather than extrapolating across them. Use [explicit homologs](#homology)
when the locus selection comes from declared feature/cluster evidence.

### Check your result {#views-check-result}
Inspect cropping reports, break markers and source coordinates. Omitted gaps have no mapping; a display flip alone is not evidence of inversion.

## 2.6 Complete collinear showcase {#collinear}

<div class="lesson-intro">The complete Module II result: four real genomes, strand-separated features and outward-routed cross-row links.</div>

### Complete result {#collinear-overview}
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/showcasecollinear.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/showcasecollinear.jpg" alt="Four-genome collinearity: strand-separated features and routed cross-row links" width="1728" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Four-genome collinearity: strand-separated features and routed cross-row links · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Collinearity extends the chord coordinate grammar; reusing data and layers is the goal. Read [inputs](#collinear-data), [coordinate replacement](#collinear-build) and [routes/ruler](#collinear-routing), then run the complete example. The identity scale and feature candidates are shared with the chord example; this linear composition omits two crowded short candidates, displaying 16 CDS with labels, with positive and negative strands above/below backbones.

### Prepare original records {#collinear-prepare}
Extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) and install dplyr, purrr and tidyr first:

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-49, eval=FALSE}
# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")

sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)

  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),

  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

```

</details>

```{r example-50, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
# Original repository records; extract the tutorial input bundle first.
show_sequences <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna") |>
  select(accver, length)
show_annotations <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep")
show_genes <- show_annotations |>
  filter(type == "CDS") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
show_alignments <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv")
# At most three substantial observed HSPs per pair; no coordinates are invented.
show_links <- show_alignments |>
  filter(length >= 900, pident >= 75) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Select up to four source CDS per sequence, spread across annotation order.
# No feature is moved or invented; keep complete source tables separately.
show_features <- show_genes |>
  filter(end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(display_bin = ntile(row_number(), 4), informative = !is.na(anno) & anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  group_by(accver, display_bin) |>
  arrange(desc(informative), desc(end - start), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno)
# Also retain well-separated negative-strand CDS, if not already represented.
show_reverse <- show_genes |>
  filter(strand == "-", end - start + 1 >= 500) |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  arrange(start, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(c(1, n())) |>
  ungroup()
show_features <- bind_rows(show_features, show_reverse) |>
  distinct(accver, start, end, strand, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(accver, start)
show_labels <- show_features
show_optimization <- optimize_ggchord_layout(
  show_sequences, show_links,
  optimize = "orientation", weight = "length"
)
```


Retain four full FASTA records, 266 CDS and 32 original HSPs. Adjacent rows use the explicitly selected observations; each non-neighbour pair retains only its longest HSP to reduce overlap.

### Reserve space for connections and labels {#collinear-gc}
The flagship no longer includes GC tracks; composition analysis remains in [tracks](#tracks). This keeps two different reading tasks from competing in the entry figure.

### Compose the layers {#collinear-compose}

```{r example-51, eval=FALSE}
# Omit two short, crowded candidates from this linear display only.
# Both source rows remain in show_features and in the chord display.
show_linear_features <- show_features |>
  filter(!anno %in% c("tail assembly protein", "gp4 protein"))
# Separate adjacent and cross-row links, retaining original endpoint values.
show_pair_rows <- show_links |>
  mutate(
    query_row = match(qaccver, show_sequences$accver),
    subject_row = match(saccver, show_sequences$accver),
    span = abs(query_row - subject_row)
  )
show_adjacent <- show_pair_rows |> filter(span == 1)
# One longest observed HSP per non-neighbour pair keeps the long routes legible.
show_cross <- show_pair_rows |>
  filter(span > 1) |>
  group_by(qaccver, saccver) |>
  slice_max(length, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()
# Inspect a backbone-only layout using the same alignment and gap as the final view.
show_linear_coord <- coord_collinear(align = "center", orientation = "auto", ratio = 0.7)
show_routing_base <- ggchord(show_sequences, show_links) +
  geom_seq(seq_gap = 0.42) + show_linear_coord
show_reference <- get_chord_layout(show_routing_base)$sequence_reference
# Shared controls sit just beyond the intervening backbones, rather than far away.
show_cross_controls <- map2(show_cross$query_row, show_cross$subject_row, function(query_row, subject_row) {
  between <- seq(min(query_row, subject_row) + 1L, max(query_row, subject_row) - 1L)
  middle_ids <- show_sequences$accver[between]
  right_edge <- max(show_reference$x_offset[middle_ids] + show_reference$lens[middle_ids] * show_reference$x_scale)
  middle_y <- mean(show_reference$y[show_sequences$accver[c(query_row, subject_row)]])
  c(right_edge + if (abs(query_row - subject_row) == 3) 0.85 else 0.65, middle_y)
})
p_show_collinear <- ggchord(show_sequences, gene_data = show_linear_features) +
  geom_link_ribbon(
    aes(ribbon_fill = pident),
    data = show_adjacent,
    link_avoid = "smooth", alpha = 0.48, linewidth = 0.22
  ) +
  geom_link_ribbon(
    aes(ribbon_fill = pident),
    data = show_cross,
    adjacent_only = FALSE, link_ctrl_point = show_cross_controls,
    link_avoid = "smooth", alpha = 0.28, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_seq(seq_gap = 0.42, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_gene(position = position_strand(0.09), width = 0.045) +
  geom_gene_label_repel(
    data = show_linear_features |> arrange(desc(nchar(anno)), accver, start),
    label_layout = "auto", label_wrap = 24,
    label_side = "auto", position = position_strand(0.09), size = 3.3
  ) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  geom_seq_scale(length = 10000, offset = unit(c(0, 10), "mm")) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(
    values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
    guide = sequence_guide
  ) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand") +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  ) +
  guides(gene_fill = strand_guide) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous(breaks = c(0, 20000, 40000, 60000, 80000), minor_breaks = NULL) +
  show_linear_coord +
  doc_theme +
  labs(
    title = "Sequence architecture, across four genomes",
    subtitle = "Selected labelled CDS · strand-separated arrows · routed cross-row comparisons"
  )
p_show_collinear
```


Dashed outlines identify non-adjacent displayed rows, with sufficient linewidth to read. Right-side controls separate long routes; smooth local clearance retreats near arrows. Identity has the same left-side colourbar as the chord view, and the bottom strand keys use arrows. The ruler's horizontal offset is 0; its length still uses the shared bp conversion.

### Adjustment and limits {#collinear-read}
Rebuild controls when changing seq_gap, order, orientation or link selection. Local arrow clearance is not an automatic route around intervening whole sequences; ribbons may still cross legitimately. Use [focus/segments](#views) for local questions. Explicit circular radius/curvature cannot currently be passed to linear coordinates; see [conversion boundaries](#collinear-data-contract).

### Save at the intended size {#collinear-save}
```{r example-52, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("four-genome-collinear.png", p_show_collinear, width = 12, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## 3.1 DNA, annotations and 13 references {#plasmid-data}

A single-sequence circular map starts with two columns. Feature, primer and restriction searches additionally need real DNA; existing annotations can be drawn directly without running recognition again.

### Tables and optional information {#plasmid-data-tables}
| Input | Required content | Optional content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backbone | accver, length; exactly one sequence | label for display; sequence for searches |
| Features | accver, start, end and declared directionality | type, anno/label, feature_id and shape categories |
| Primers | Computed binding interval, strand/name roles required by the geom | Recognition and provenance fields |
| Restriction sites | Position/name roles required by the geom | Enzyme catalogue, methylation assumption and filter provenance |

Backbones do not require DNA. Prefer search-result tables for the latter layers and consult their help for detailed fields. Unknown-strand annotations belong in generic feature layers.

### Inspect bundled real records {#plasmid-data-inspect}
```{r example-53, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
plasmid_example_pUC19 |> select(accver, length)
find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19) |> select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno) |> slice_head(n = 5)
```

The compact names retain ggchord's early BLAST workflow history. accver need not be a database accession. Full DNA and length must agree. Recognition is computational matching, not experimental validation.

### Import your own plasmid {#plasmid-data-import}
`read_fasta_lengths()` reads IDs and full lengths only. Searches additionally need actual DNA, for example read with optional Biostrings `readDNAStringSet()` and `as.character()`, retaining matching IDs. GFF3/BED/GenBank or GRanges annotations follow the [format guide](#formats), retaining provenance. Handle circular-origin and segmented records according to the reader contract; do not invent one continuous interval by merging every segment.

### A progressive case sequence {#plasmid-data-path}
[3.2](#plasmid-build) builds pUC19 layer by layer; [3.3](#recognition) explains recognition, primers and restriction sites; [3.4](#plasmid-catalog) uses all 13 unique repository plasmids; [3.5](#plasmids-complex) completes the dense pETDuet-1 map. pUC19c is a compatibility alias, not a 14th case.


## 3.2 From a circle to annotation layers {#plasmid-build}

Focus on the visual information added at each step. Preparation computes inputs; independent layers still control drawing.

### Prepare this page {#plasmid-build-prepare}
<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-54, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
feature_palette <- c(
  CDS = "#993366", promoter = "#31849B", rep_origin = "#F1E51D",
  primer_bind = "#A020F0", misc_feature = "#A6ACB3", protein_bind = "#31849B"
)

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}

library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
plasmid_feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
# Dedicated primer layers already show bindings; avoid duplicate primer annotations.
plasmid_features <- plasmid_feature_source |>
  filter(type != "primer_bind") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
plasmid_primers <- find_primer_bindings(plasmid_example_pUC19, set = "universal")
plasmid_sites <- find_restriction_sites(plasmid_example_pUC19)
display_sites <- filter_restriction_sites(plasmid_sites, enzymes = c("EcoRI", "BamHI", "HindIII"))
primer_names <- primer_catalog(set = "universal")
```

### Step 1: double backbone and centre name {#plasmid-build-backbone}
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/plasmidbackbone.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/plasmidbackbone.jpg" alt="pUC19 step1: double backbone" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 step1: double backbone · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

### Step 2: feature shapes {#plasmid-build-features}
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/plasmidfeatures.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/plasmidfeatures.jpg" alt="pUC19 step2: features" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 step2: features · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
`position_feature_stack()` separates overlaps; `geom_feature_plasmid()` selects shapes and colours by real category. Compact short-feature shapes do not imply missing data.

### Step 3: fitted feature labels {#plasmid-build-labels}
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/plasmidtext.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/plasmidtext.jpg" alt="pUC19 step3: labels" width="1440" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 step3: labels · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
Geometry and labels share a Position. Allow shrinking only above an explicit minimum and external placement when necessary; recheck after changing dimensions.

### Step 4: primers and selected restriction sites {#plasmid-build-details}

```{r example-56, eval=FALSE}
plasmid_position <- position_feature_stack(spacing = .10, base_position = position_plasmid())
p_plasmid <- ggchord(seq_data = plasmid_seq) +
  geom_seq(seq_style = "double") +
  geom_feature_plasmid(aes(feature_fill = type), data = plasmid_features, position = plasmid_position) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(
    data = plasmid_features, position = plasmid_position,
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_primer(data = plasmid_primers, colour = "#A020F0") +
  geom_primer_label_repel(data = plasmid_primers, colour = "#A020F0", max_overlaps = 0, size = 3) +
  geom_restriction_site(data = display_sites, colour = "#29364B", label_size = 3, leader = "radial") +
  geom_seq_center_label() +
  scale_feature_fill_manual(values = feature_palette) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous() +
  coord_circular(rotation = 90) +
  theme_ggchord_plasmid() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  )
p_plasmid
```

## 3.3 Features, primers and restriction {#recognition}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Search known DNA for primers, restriction sites and common features, then choose a display. Computational matches and experimental validation are different.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#recognition-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

```{r example-57, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
```

### Search and display are separate {#recognition-search}
Use the bundled pUC19 DNA for exact catalogue-primer and selected restriction searches:


```{r example-58, eval=FALSE}
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
target <- setNames(plasmid_example_pUC19$sequence, plasmid_example_pUC19$accver)
primers <- find_primer_bindings(target, set = "universal")
sites <- find_restriction_sites(target, enzymes = c("EcoRI", "BamHI", "HindIII"), methylation = "none")
recognition_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
p_sites <- ggchord(seq_data = recognition_seq) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_primer(data = primers, colour = "#A020F0") +
  geom_restriction_site(data = sites, colour = "#29364B") +
  coord_circular()
p_sites
```


Search supports circular-origin binding; set `circular = FALSE` for a linear sequence.
The actual pUC19 hits shown here should be inspected in the returned table. Search hits are computational matches, not experimental validation.
Primer `"three_prime"` mode finds an exact suffix, with no mismatch model;
its Wallace melting-temperature estimate is a composition heuristic.

### Restriction interpretation {#recognition-restriction}
`find_restriction_sites()` returns unfiltered matches and cleavage coordinates;
`filter_restriction_sites()` selects a display set. Enzyme site counts refer to
the full supplied sequence and remain stable after filtering. `methylation =
"auto"` uses audited context only for exactly recognized bundled references;
it does not claim unknown samples are unblocked. This example explicitly uses `"none"`; this is a search assumption, not a measurement
of methylation in a physical sample. `geom_restriction_site(leader = "radial")` is the default route.

### General feature recognition {#recognition-features}
`find_common_features()` supports curated exact-reference annotations, DNA and
record-specific matching modes. Protein searches use standard-code six-frame
translation; they do not implement splicing, alternative initiation or
origin-crossing protein matches. Source genetic-code metadata does not select
another translation table. For nonstandard codes use DNA matching or external
code-aware analysis. Confidence is a heuristic label, not a probability.
Use [explicit CDS projection](#projection) for known protein/genome maps.

### Follow an annotated reference workflow {#recognition-reference}
This short workflow uses the same source-backed plasmid as the complete map. The [complete pUC19
workflow](#plasmids) demonstrates catalogue annotations, exact reference
matching, site display filtering, primer labels and feature stacking together.
Changing only a sequence name does not make it a recognized reference; sequence
content determines source-backed recognition. Read the result methods and
methylation provenance instead of assigning reference claims to an unknown sample.

### Check your result {#recognition-check-result}
Inspect match positions, methods and provenance. Restriction filtering is a display choice; methylation search conditions are not a measurement of an unknown sample.

```{r example-60, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
# Thirteen unique records; the compatibility spelling pUC19c is not an extra plasmid.
catalog_objects <- c(
  "plasmid_example_pSB1C3", "plasmid_example_pUC19", "plasmid_example_pBR322",
  "plasmid_example_pBluescript_II_SK_plus", "plasmid_example_pET_28a_plus",
  "plasmid_example_pETDuet_1", "plasmid_example_pDONR221",
  "plasmid_example_pcDNA3_1_plus", "plasmid_example_pTRE_Tight_BI",
  "plasmid_example_pTRIPZ", "plasmid_example_pCAMBIA1300",
  "plasmid_example_pEarleyGate_201", "plasmid_example_pSpCas9_BB_2A_GFP_PX458"
)
read_catalog_record <- function(object) {
  target <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  data(list = object, package = "ggchord", envir = target)
  target[[object]]
}
catalog_sequences <- map(catalog_objects, read_catalog_record)
catalog_features <- map(catalog_sequences, find_common_features)
catalog_summary <- map2(catalog_sequences, catalog_features, function(sequence, features) {
  tibble(accver = sequence$accver, length = sequence$length, features = nrow(features))
}) |>
  bind_rows()
```


```{r example-61, eval=FALSE}
make_catalog_plot <- function(sequence, features) {
  placement <- position_feature_stack(spacing = 0.085, base_position = position_plasmid())
  ggchord(seq_data = sequence |> select(accver, length)) +
    geom_seq(seq_style = "double", colour = "#252525") +
    geom_feature_plasmid(data = features, position = placement) +
    geom_feature_label_repel(
      data = features, position = placement, external = FALSE,
      label_fit = "shrink", label_min_size = 2.5, max_overlaps = 0
    ) +
    geom_seq_center_label() +
    coord_circular(rotation = 90, fit = "manual", xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.35, 1.35)) +
    theme_ggchord_plasmid() +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA)
    )
}
catalog_plots <- map2(catalog_sequences, catalog_features, make_catalog_plot)
names(catalog_plots) <- catalog_summary$accver
# Save any record at the same size used in the gallery.
# ggsave("pBR322.png", catalog_plots[["pBR322"]], width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 144)
```


One small function composes independent layers, retaining every recognition result in catalog_features. Actual counts appear below. These maps retain all feature geometry and fit labels inside, allowing labels to hide when space is insufficient; primers and dense restriction annotations are combined in the [complete case](#plasmids-complex). Save a named plot with the commented ggsave call.

## 3.5 Complete plasmid cases {#plasmids}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Build a readable plasmid map from bundled pUC19 DNA, with separate annotation, primer and restriction layers. Keep display choices separate from complete results.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#plasmids-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-62, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
feature_palette <- c(
  CDS = "#993366", promoter = "#31849B", rep_origin = "#F1E51D",
  primer_bind = "#A020F0", misc_feature = "#A6ACB3", protein_bind = "#31849B"
)

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
```
