```{r example-62, eval=FALSE}
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}
```

</details>

The preparation above declares the palette and shared appearance.

### Use a source-backed sequence {#plasmids-input}
The bundled `plasmid_example_pUC19` is copied from the repository's original
`examples/plasmid/pUC19.fna`; bases and sequence identity are not edited for display.
The workflow uses the package's source-backed recognition catalogues. It needs no
network request or experimental measurements fabricated for the figure.


```{r example-63, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
plasmid_feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
# Dedicated primer layers already show bindings; avoid duplicate primer annotations.
plasmid_features <- plasmid_feature_source |>
  filter(type != "primer_bind") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
plasmid_primers <- find_primer_bindings(plasmid_example_pUC19, set = "universal")
plasmid_sites <- find_restriction_sites(plasmid_example_pUC19)
display_sites <- filter_restriction_sites(plasmid_sites, enzymes = c("EcoRI", "BamHI", "HindIII"))
primer_names <- primer_catalog(set = "universal")
```


Inspect `plasmid_features`, `plasmid_primers` and `display_sites` to distinguish complete search results from display choices.

### Compose independent layers {#plasmids-draw}
Add the backbone, annotations, labels, primers and restriction sites in that order. Features and their labels share one Position; each layer reads its own data.


```{r example-64, eval=FALSE}
plasmid_position <- position_feature_stack(spacing = .10, base_position = position_plasmid())
p_plasmid <- ggchord(seq_data = plasmid_seq) +
  geom_seq(seq_style = "double") +
  geom_feature_plasmid(aes(feature_fill = type), data = plasmid_features, position = plasmid_position) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(
    data = plasmid_features, position = plasmid_position,
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_primer(data = plasmid_primers, colour = "#A020F0") +
  geom_primer_label_repel(data = plasmid_primers, colour = "#A020F0", max_overlaps = 0, size = 3) +
  geom_restriction_site(data = display_sites, colour = "#29364B", label_size = 3, leader = "radial") +
  geom_seq_center_label() +
  scale_feature_fill_manual(values = feature_palette) +
  scale_seq_position_continuous() +
  coord_circular(rotation = 90) +
  theme_ggchord_plasmid() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  )
p_plasmid
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/plasmid.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/plasmid.jpg" alt="pUC19 features, exact primer hits and three selected restriction sites" width="1440" height="1296" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 features, exact primer hits and three selected restriction sites · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Full sequence length (bp) | 2686 |
| Annotation rows | 7 |
| Exact primer hit records | 6 |
| Enzyme match records (not distinct positions) | 49845 |
| Restriction records selected for display | 3 |

Mixed exterior annotations share root-ordered placement, including sparse restriction labels beside primers. This example uses the dedicated plasmid theme and default feature fitting: internal text is tried before adjacent/external placement. Inspect at the final export dimensions instead of hiding crossings by shrinking text or forcing offsets.


The original annotation table is retained in `plasmid_feature_source`. Dedicated
primer layers replace duplicate `primer_bind` annotations in the displayed feature
table; only geometry, type and annotation text are passed to feature layers.

### Read the annotation layers {#plasmids-layers}
The double backbone establishes one circular sequence. General features use a
plasmid preset and explicit stacking Position; labels use the same Position.
Primer arcs indicate binding ranges, restriction ticks indicate cleavage/display
positions, and the centre label identifies the sequence and length. A cropped or
filtered display does not change the full-sequence restriction count.

### Choose the displayed sites deliberately {#plasmids-sites}
`find_restriction_sites()` returns all matches. This figure explicitly selects
EcoRI, BamHI and HindIII so that a compact restriction cluster remains readable;
`plasmid_sites` retains the complete search result. The `reference` filter uses a saved
reference display set only when the complete supplied sequence matches that
reference. Other tasks can select `unique`, `six_plus` or explicit enzyme names.
Inspect `display_sites` and the site's methylation/source columns before drawing.
The reference set is a presentation choice, not a claim about an unknown sample.

### Understand catalogue and label limits {#plasmids-limits}
`primer_names` exposes catalogue entries. This example searches the universal catalogue exactly; reference primer
annotations and exact oligonucleotide searches have distinct provenance. Near-exact protein feature
recognition has the limitations in [recognition](#recognition); it does not
validate biological function or a primer experiment. Text can move, shrink within
its explicit minimum, or hide. Keep the geometry and inspect exported label
reasons at the final size rather than assuming every annotation must have text.

### Adapt the workflow {#plasmids-adapt}
For your own named DNA sequence, replace the input and inspect search results
before adding geoms. For externally curated annotations, pass your feature table
instead of running recognition. Use [stacking and shapes](#annotations) for
geometry, [labels](#labels) for fitting, and [output](#output) for devices.

`geom_primer_label_repel(side = "inside")` keeps callouts inside the backbone,
even alongside exterior restriction and feature labels. This is corrected in the
0.16.6 release; v0.16.5 can move those requested inside labels
outside. The default outside placement and existing source coordinates are unchanged.

Inside restriction labels also retain their inner geometry and now report the
inner side in the exported annotation registry; earlier versions mislabelled
those diagnostic rows as exterior resources.

The full inside scene can still place long primer text over other feature regions.
The default `max_overlaps = Inf` does not certify zero overlap across feature
layers. Prefer the default outside field when space is tight, or use
`show_location = FALSE` to shorten the display; inspect the result at its final size.

### Check your result {#plasmids-check-result}
Start with the centre name and length, then read positions, category colours, arrow directions and outer labels. Check enzyme names in display_sites; selecting a display subset leaves plasmid_sites intact.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#labels">Labels and local placement →</a></div>

### Save this result {#plasmids-save-result}
Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

```{r example-65, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("pUC19-map.png", p_plasmid, width = 10, height = 9, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```

### Complete example: a dense pETDuet-1 map {#plasmids-complex}

Use the pUC19 example above to learn the layers, then move to the richer pETDuet-1 map. Inputs come from the bundled sequence, feature and reference-primer catalogues. The restriction subset retains unique six-base-or-longer recognition sites from commercial_all; it is not every cut made by every enzyme.


```{r example-66, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
show_plasmid <- plasmid_example_pETDuet_1 |>
  select(accver, length)
show_plasmid_features <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
show_plasmid_primers <- find_primer_bindings(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1, set = "reference")
show_plasmid_all_sites <- find_restriction_sites(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
show_plasmid_sites <- filter_restriction_sites(
  show_plasmid_all_sites,
  set = "unique_6plus", parent_set = "commercial_all"
)
```



```{r example-67, eval=FALSE}
show_plasmid_position <- position_feature_stack(
  spacing = 0.085, base_position = position_plasmid()
)
p_show_plasmid <- ggchord(show_plasmid, validate = "none") +
  geom_seq(seq_style = "double", colour = "#252525") +
  geom_feature_plasmid(data = show_plasmid_features, position = show_plasmid_position) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(
    data = show_plasmid_features, position = show_plasmid_position,
    external = TRUE, max_overlaps = 0,
    label_fit = "shrink", label_min_size = 2.5
  ) +
  geom_primer(data = show_plasmid_primers, colour = "#A020F0") +
  geom_primer_label_repel(
    data = show_plasmid_primers, colour = "#A020F0", max_overlaps = 0
  ) +
  geom_restriction_site(data = show_plasmid_sites, colour = "#252525") +
  geom_seq_center_label() +
  coord_circular(
    rotation = 90, fit = "manual",
    xlim = c(-3.4, 4.6), ylim = c(-1.6, 2.4)
  ) +
  theme_ggchord_plasmid() +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  )
p_show_plasmid
```


<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/showcaseplasmid.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/showcaseplasmid.jpg" alt="Dense pETDuet-1 map: features, reference primers and grouped restriction sites" width="2376" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Dense pETDuet-1 map: features, reference primers and grouped restriction sites · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Inputs contain 20 features, five reference primers and 58 grouped cut positions. The feature preset retains plum coding regions, mint resistance genes, yellow origins and blue regulatory features; primers are purple, consistently across this site. Dense labels depend on export size; open the full image to read them.

The explicit viewport keeps the dense map at the documented export size. `label_fit = "shrink"` allows short-feature labels to fit down to 2.5 mm; labels that do not fit remain callouts. Preview and save at the same 16.5 × 8 in size.

```{r example-68, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("pETDuet-1-map.png", p_show_plasmid, width = 16.5, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```


## Prepare tables and coordinates {#data}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Turn file observations into plotting roles. Check minimal fields and coordinates, then use validation reports to decide on cleaning; do not guess missing lengths or strands.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#data-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed. For file-based examples, first extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) so the working directory contains `examples/`.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-69, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)
```

</details>

### Tables {#data-tables}
| Input | Required fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sequence | `accver`, `length` | Unique ID; positive full length in bp |
| Interval link | `qaccver`, `saccver`, `qstart`, `qend`, `sstart`, `send` | Query and subject anchors |
| Gene | `accver`, `start`, `end`, `strand` | Known `+`/`-`; optional `anno` |
| Feature | `accver`, `start`, `end`, `strand` or declared direction | May retain unknown strand; optional `type`, `label`, `feature_id` |

Identifiers may be arbitrary strings. Accession versions are preserved exactly.
`pident` and alignment `length` are optional unless a mapping, filter or statistic
needs them. A feature interval does not imply a sequence's full length.

### Coordinate contract {#data-coordinates}
Genomic coordinates are **one-based, inclusive bp**. BED/PAF readers convert their
source conventions; do not convert twice. Gene endpoints are ordered with
strand stored separately; link endpoint order may encode direction. A one-bp
link without direction evidence stays unknown. Unknown strand is never silently
changed to `+`; use `geom_feature()` instead of the strict gene layer.

Amino-acid coordinates require [explicit CDS projection](#projection).
Native Cartesian layout units, genomic bp, angles in degrees, physical mm and
track value units are different domains. See the full
data contract (`help("ggchord_data_contract", package = "ggchord")`).

### Import original records {#data-import}
Run this repository-only example from its root. Original files are not rewritten.


```{r example-70, eval=FALSE}
seq_files <- read_fasta_lengths(files = "examples/fasta/*.fna", source_file = TRUE)
link_files <- read_blast(files = "examples/blastn-standard/*.tsv", source_file = TRUE)
feature_files <- read_gff3(files = "examples/gff3/*.gff3", unstranded = "keep", source_file = TRUE)
```


`read_genbank()` retains record/feature provenance and segmented locations.
`read_bed()` and `read_paf()` retain their conversion metadata. `as_ggchord_seq()`,
`as_ggchord_feature()` and `as_ggchord_link()` adapt supported S4 objects; provide
full lengths and IDs explicitly when the object lacks them. `file` and `files` both accept path vectors or globs; repeated resolved paths
are read once in first-occurrence order. Choose one clear entry for a workflow. Missing sequence or
homology data must be supplied by the analyst, not invented by the plotting layer.

### Validate, clean, prepare {#data-validation}
After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-71, eval=FALSE}
validation <- validate_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes)
cleaned <- clean_ggchord_data(seqs, links, genes)
prepared <- prepare_ggchord_data(seqs, links, features = list(genes = genes))
```


Validation reports issues; cleaning makes explicit repairs with a report.
Preparation combines workflow steps without inferring biological membership.
Inspect `validation`, `cleaned$report` and `prepared$report` before plotting.
`source_row` in geometry refers to the resolved layer input, while `.source_line`
means a physical file line; GenBank has separate record/feature provenance.
Aggregates may have `source_rows` and `.length_estimated` flags. Preserve these
when filtering or merging links.

### Inspect a problematic input and its repair report {#data-repairs}

```{r example-72, eval=FALSE}
# Deliberately corrupt copies to demonstrate diagnostics; original rows remain intact.
problem_links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  slice_head(n = 2) |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send, pident) |>
  mutate(
    qaccver = replace(qaccver, 2, "absent"),
    pident = replace(pident, 1, 103)
  )
problem_report <- validate_ggchord_data(seqs, problem_links)
repaired <- clean_ggchord_data(seqs, problem_links, unknown_id = "drop", invalid_pident = "clip")
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Input rows | 2 |
| Rows retained after explicit cleaning | 1 |

The demonstration intentionally includes an unknown ID and
identity outside 0–100 in copied source rows. These explicit repairs are not a recommendation to clip
scientific observations silently. Inspect `problem_report` and `repaired$report`,
retain the original table, and choose policies appropriate to actual evidence.
A legitimate reverse alignment can keep endpoint order instead of being sorted.
`prepare_ggchord_data()` therefore retains its workflow-specific default policy;
standalone cleaning and preparation should not be assumed identical.

### Declare genome and contig keys {#data-hierarchy}

```{r example-73, eval=FALSE}
# Each source record represents a separate complete phage genome.
contigs <- seqs |>
  mutate(genome = accver)
genomes <- tibble(genome = seqs$accver)
hierarchy <- validate_ggchord_hierarchy(contigs, genomes, strict = TRUE)
```


`hierarchy$contigs` summarizes declared membership without concatenating contigs.
No membership is inferred from an accession prefix. Provide globally unique IDs
when separate samples reuse local contig names. Use [file formats and adapters](#formats)
for format/optional-object details, and the [real-record tutorial](#real-data)
to carry reports into a complete figure.

### Minimal input and protein alignments {#data-minimal}
| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Sequence columns passed to the plot | 2 |
| Link columns passed to the plot | 6 |
| Gene columns passed to the plot | 4 |

The second positional constructor argument is `ribbon_data`, not `gene_data`.
Use explicit argument names as in the shared examples. Optional identity, length
and coverage fields are needed only by operations that consume them. See
[standard BLAST/protein input](#alignments) and [parameter formats](#parameters).

### Check your result {#data-check-result}
Input IDs must match complete sequence records. Keep original records separate from repaired copies. Decreasing endpoints can be legitimate reverse hits; warnings do not all mean rows must be removed.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#formats">File formats and explicit adapters →</a></div>


## Import and convert data {#formats}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Convert tables, BED, PAF or GenBank into ggchord inputs while retaining record identity and converting coordinate conventions only once.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#formats-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed. For file-based examples, first extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) so the working directory contains `examples/`.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-74, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}

library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
features <- feature_source |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
```

</details>

### Adapt an existing table {#formats-adapters}
The preparation above loads the input tables. These examples rename columns of
bundled source-backed sequences, links and genes; they do not invent alignments.


```{r example-75, eval=FALSE}
renamed_sequences <- seqs |>
  rename(chrom = accver, size = length)
sequence_input <- as_ggchord_seq(renamed_sequences, mapping = c(accver = "chrom", length = "size"))
renamed_features <- genes |>
  rename(chrom = accver, left = start, right = end)
feature_input <- as_ggchord_feature(renamed_features,
  mapping = c(accver = "chrom", start = "left", end = "right")
)
link_input <- as_ggchord_link(links)
```


Adapters return ordinary frames with `ggchord_conversion` provenance. IDs remain
unchanged. Supply reliable full lengths rather than using maximum feature ends.
See [alignment input](#alignments) for minimal fields and coordinate units.

### BED and PAF: convert coordinates once {#formats-zero-based}
The BED example writes known pUC19 intervals as minimal BED3 and reads them back.
PAF comes directly from real minimap2 output in the public tutorial, with original
optional tags/values. The display retains mapq ≥30 and receives only six endpoint roles.


```{r example-76, eval=FALSE}
# BED3 carries intervals only; the source annotations remain in features.
bed_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".bed")
bed_rows <- tibble(accver = features$accver, start0 = features$start - 1L, end = features$end)
write.table(bed_rows, bed_path, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
bed_features <- read_bed(bed_path)
unlink(bed_path)
# Unchanged PAF rows from the public EMALE tutorial, not a simulated alignment.
paf_source <- read_paf("examples/format-inputs/emales-pair.paf")
paf_selected <- paf_source |>
  filter(!is.na(mapq), mapq >= 30)
paf_links <- paf_selected |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
paf_seqs <- bind_rows(
  transmute(paf_source, accver = qaccver, length = qlen),
  transmute(paf_source, accver = saccver, length = slen)
) |>
  distinct()
p_paf <- ggchord(seq_data = paf_seqs, ribbon_data = paf_links) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#6BAFA6", alpha = .5) +
  geom_seq(colour = "#233E4A") +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis() +
  doc_theme
p_paf
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/paf.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/paf.jpg" alt="A real minimap2 PAF comparison between two EMALE genomes" width="1440" height="720" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>A real minimap2 PAF comparison between two EMALE genomes · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

The reader converts BED zero-based half-open intervals to one-based inclusive
coordinates; do not add one again. BED3 has no strand, so it returns unknown
strand; use a strand-bearing format when needed. Negative PAF relative direction
becomes decreasing subject endpoints. These are valid reverse hits, not values
to sort indiscriminately. Quality/identity use producer fields, not new alignments.

### GenBank: retain record identity {#formats-genbank}

```{r example-77, eval=FALSE}
# The original NCBI L09137.2 record identifies pUC19c; keep that identity.
genbank_result <- NULL
if (nzchar(Sys.which("python3")) && identical(suppressWarnings(system2("python3",
  c("-c", shQuote("from Bio import SeqIO")),
  stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE
)), 0L)) {
  genbank_result <- read_genbank("examples/format-inputs/pUC19c-L09137.2.gb")
}
```


This is the original NCBI L09137.2 record, named pUC19c; do not rename it to the
bundled pUC19. Results include `seq_data`, `features$annotation` and `report`,
retaining segmented locations and record/feature provenance. The selected Python
needs Biopython already installed; no automatic installation occurs.
`unsupported = "report"` records unsupported locations rather than guessing bounds.

### Optional interval objects {#formats-ranges}

```{r example-78, eval=FALSE}
range_inputs <- NULL
if (requireNamespace("GenomicRanges", quietly = TRUE)) {
  unknown <- features |>
    filter(strand == ".") |>
    slice_head(n = 1)
  ranges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
    seqnames = unknown$accver,
    ranges = IRanges::IRanges(unknown$start, unknown$end), strand = "*",
    seqlengths = setNames(plasmid_seq$length, plasmid_seq$accver)
  )
  range_inputs <- list(seq_data = as_ggchord_seq(ranges), features = as_ggchord_feature(ranges))
}
```



```{r example-79, eval=FALSE}
interaction_inputs <- NULL
if (requireNamespace("GenomicRanges", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("InteractionSet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  source_links <- ribbon_data_example |>
    slice_head(n = 2)
  lengths <- setNames(seq_data_example$length, seq_data_example$accver)
  query <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
    seqnames = source_links$qaccver,
    ranges = IRanges::IRanges(
      pmin(source_links$qstart, source_links$qend),
      pmax(source_links$qstart, source_links$qend)
    ),
    strand = ifelse(source_links$qstart <= source_links$qend, "+", "-"),
    seqlengths = lengths
  )
  subject <- GenomicRanges::GRanges(
    seqnames = source_links$saccver,
    ranges = IRanges::IRanges(
      pmin(source_links$sstart, source_links$send),
      pmax(source_links$sstart, source_links$send)
    ),
    strand = ifelse(source_links$sstart <= source_links$send, "+", "-"),
    seqlengths = lengths
  )
  interactions <- InteractionSet::GInteractions(query, subject)
  interaction_inputs <- list(
    seq_data = as_ggchord_seq(interactions),
    ribbon_data = as_ggchord_link(interactions)
  )
}
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| GenBank optional reader | SKIP: Biopython unavailable |
| Optional interval adapter | PASS |
| Optional GInteractions adapter | PASS |

An originally unknown-strand pUC19 annotation remains unknown as `*`. Known full
lengths populate Seqinfo. `GInteractions` can become links but still needs explicit
sequence/length context. Missing dependencies are marked skipped, not validated
by source presence. See the data contract (`help("ggchord_data_contract", package = "ggchord")`).
SAM/BAM CIGAR is not parsed directly: use an alignment-aware tool before table
adaptation; renaming columns alone cannot resolve splicing.

### Check your result {#formats-check-result}
Inspect returned fields and conversion reports before selecting plotting fields. Preserve endpoint direction for reverse PAF hits; do not rename a GenBank record to pretend it is a different bundled plasmid.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#alignments">Import nucleotide and protein alignments →</a></div>


## Import nucleotide and protein alignments {#alignments}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Use standard BLAST tabular output without the historical custom 17-column layout. Distinguish file fields, minimal plotting roles and nucleotide versus protein units.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#alignments-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed. For file-based examples, first extract the [input bundle](https://github.com/DangJem/ggchord/tree/main/examples) so the working directory contains `examples/`.

```{r example-80, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
```

### Use the default tabular columns {#alignments-standard}
The historical custom list of 17 fields is unnecessary. Use standard tabular output:

```sh
blastn -query query.fna -subject subject.fna -outfmt 6 -out result.tsv
blastp -query proteins.faa -subject reference.faa -outfmt 7 -out result.tsv
```

Format `6` is a table; `7` adds comments. Without a custom field list both use
12 default fields. Omitting `-outfmt` entirely produces pairwise text, which this
tabular reader does not parse. Fields are query ID, subject ID, pident, length,
mismatch, gapopen, qstart, qend, sstart, send, evalue, bitscore. Their identifier
roles become `qaccver`/`saccver`; values are preserved and need not be accession versions.
See the [NCBI format documentation](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK279684/table/appendices.T.options_common_to_all_blast/).

### File layout and minimal plotting fields differ {#alignments-minimal}
Twelve file columns do not require twelve plotting columns. After the
preparation code above, try the source-backed records:


```{r example-81, eval=FALSE}
blast_source <- read_blast("examples/blastn-standard/MT108731.1__MT118296.1.tsv")
blast_links <- blast_source |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# A six-column table is sufficient for drawing; extra fields stay in blast_source.
custom_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
write.table(blast_links, custom_path, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
custom_source <- read_blast(custom_path, format = "custom", col_names = names(blast_links))
custom_links <- custom_source |>
  select(all_of(names(blast_links)))
unlink(custom_path)
```


`blast_source` retains statistics and provenance; `blast_links` has six endpoint roles.
Identity requires `pident` only when mapped/filtered; alignment-length filters or
weights require `length`. `qlen`/`slen` support the corresponding coverage calculations.
They are not general plotting requirements. A custom headerless layout requires
explicit `col_names`; arbitrary six-column meanings are not guessed.
Use `as_ggchord_link(x, mapping = ...)` for an already-read non-BLAST table;
see [format conversion](#formats-adapters).

Files in `examples/blastn-standard/` retain historical HSP rows and their first
12 values. They are column conversions, not new BLAST runs. Old `.o7` inputs are
unchanged; the conversion script and hashes record that distinction.

### Read BLASTp with explicit coordinate units {#alignments-protein}
This real BLASTP 2.9.0+ output and query CDS annotation come from the public
EMALE tutorial. Retain the original table, then select sufficiently long,
low-evalue query HSPs with complete known CDS mappings.


```{r example-82, eval=FALSE}
protein_source <- read_blast("examples/format-inputs/emales-mavirus-blastp.tsv", source_file = TRUE)
emale_source <- read_gff3("examples/format-inputs/emales-BVI_023A.gff3", source_file = TRUE)
# The source declares complete Prodigal CDS and translation table 11.
emale_coding <- emale_source |>
  filter(grepl("partial=00", attributes)) |>
  select(feature_id, accver, start, end, strand, phase)
emale_cds <- build_ggchord_cds(emale_coding, genetic_code = 11)
# Keep strong HSPs whose query protein has a known complete CDS.
# Gaps are retained: projecting one query span does not assert an ungapped pair.
protein_kept <- protein_source |>
  filter(qaccver %in% emale_coding$feature_id, evalue <= 1e-10, length >= 50) |>
  arrange(desc(bitscore))
selected_hsp <- protein_kept |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
query_interval <- tibble(
  feature_id = "query_HSP", parent_id = selected_hsp$qaccver,
  start = selected_hsp$qstart, end = selected_hsp$qend
)
projected_query <- project_ggchord_features(query_interval, emale_cds)
# Subject projection additionally requires its own CDS map; it is not guessed from an accession.
```

| Metric | Observed output |
| --- | --- |
| Original BLASTp HSPs | 2948 |
| Complete query CDS records | 24 |
| Query HSPs retained by the explicit filter | 3 |
| Selected query start (aa) | 50 |
| Selected query end (aa) | 289 |
| Projected query-span rows | 1 |

BLASTp endpoints are amino-acid coordinates. This example projects the query HSP
span into the known CDS's genomic coordinates, retaining strand and phase.
A gapped HSP still has a projectable query span; that envelope is not a base-by-base
nucleotide correspondence. Weak hits, gap counts and statistics remain in the source.

Projecting both ends requires the subject's own CDS map. It cannot be inferred
from an accession, maximum endpoint or annotation name. The `ungapped = TRUE`
assertion for `project_ggchord_links()` needs evidence. The [projection tutorial](#projection)
uses two real plasmid CDS with identical oriented DNA to demonstrate a justified
ungapped two-ended case.

Native protein backbones with aa axes are outside this version. For `blastx` and
`tblastn`, check each endpoint's units independently. Parsing does not establish
that a table can be drawn directly in genomic bp coordinates.

### Sources and limits {#alignments-source}
Original EMALE records come from the [public gggenomes data/tutorial](https://thackl.github.io/gggenomes/articles/emales.html).
Only data records are reused; all figures are drawn with ggchord, without copying
upstream figures or plotting code. The input bundle's `sources.json` records URLs,
archive members, line ranges, hashes and selection. Parsing neither reruns
alignments nor establishes biological function.

### Check your result {#alignments-check-result}
A basic link table needs six fields. BLASTp reading retains aa coordinates; use a supported CDS mapping before drawing on this version’s bp axes.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#projection">CDS coordinate projection →</a></div>


## Project protein intervals to genomic coordinates {#projection}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Project known protein intervals to genomic positions through real CDS, retaining phase, strand and segmentation explicitly.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#projection-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-83, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}

library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
data(plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_source <- bind_rows(plasmid_example_pUC19, plasmid_example_pETDuet_1)
homolog_seq <- homolog_source |>
  select(accver, length)
cluster_features <- homolog_source |>
  find_common_features() |>
  filter(type == "CDS", anno == "AmpR") |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, anno) |>
  arrange(match(accver, homolog_source$accver)) |>
  mutate(feature_id = paste(accver, start, end, sep = ":"))
# Membership is computed from exact strand-corrected CDS DNA equality, not gene names.
reverse_complement <- function(sequence) {
  bases <- strsplit(sequence, "")[[1]]
  chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", paste(rev(bases), collapse = ""))
}
coding_sequences <- cluster_features |>
  left_join(select(homolog_source, accver, sequence), by = "accver") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    coding_dna = substr(sequence, start, end),
    coding_dna = if (strand == "-") reverse_complement(coding_dna) else coding_dna
  ) |>
  ungroup()
cds_dna <- pull(coding_sequences, coding_dna)

membership <- tibble(
  feature_id = cluster_features$feature_id,
  cluster_id = paste0("exact_CDS_", match(cds_dna, unique(cds_dna)))
)
homologs <- link_ggchord_clusters(cluster_features, membership,
  pairs = tibble(qaccver = homolog_seq$accver[1], saccver = homolog_seq$accver[2])
)
loci <- find_ggchord_loci(homolog_seq, cluster_features,
  targets = cluster_features$feature_id[cluster_features$anno == "AmpR"][1], upstream = 100, downstream = 100
)

# Compare equivalent local windows instead of shrinking one gene on full plasmids.
homolog_windows <- cluster_features |>
  select(accver, start, end)
local_homologs <- focus_ggchord_data(homolog_seq, homologs$data, cluster_features,
  loci = homolog_windows, expand = 200
)
p_homologs <- ggchord(
  seq_data = local_homologs$seq_data,
  ribbon_data = local_homologs$ribbon_data, gene_data = local_homologs$gene_data
) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#269B82", alpha = .65) +
  geom_seq(colour = "#233E4A", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_feature(
    data = local_homologs$gene_data, feature_fill = "#F1D334",
    position = position_strand(.10), width = .07
  ) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = local_homologs$gene_data, size = 4, label_fit = "shrink") +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  geom_seq_break() +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis("source") +
  doc_theme
p_homologs
```

</details>

### Start with source-backed CDS {#projection-cds}
Run the [identical-CDS comparison](#homology-membership) first. It uses real
bundled plasmid annotations and DNA. Complete CDS use explicit phase 0 and
translation table 11.


```{r example-84, eval=FALSE}
# Run the exact-CDS comparison first; these are complete source-backed CDS.
coding <- cluster_features |>
  mutate(phase = 0)
cds <- build_ggchord_cds(coding, genetic_code = 11)
# This selects residues for a display example; it does not claim a detected domain.
domains <- tibble(feature_id = "selected_residues", parent_id = coding$feature_id[1], start = 2, end = 20)
genomic <- project_ggchord_features(domains, cds)
genomic
```


This example selects residues 2–20 for display; it does not claim a detected
protein domain. Projection returns genomic intervals with strand/segment context.
Actual domains require exact parent CDS IDs and amino-acid ranges; annotation
names or maximum feature endpoints cannot supply missing evidence.

### Segments, phase and partial regions {#projection-boundaries}
`build_ggchord_cds()` constructs a segment map; `project_ggchord_features()` then
splits amino-acid intervals through it. Crossing a boundary can return several
rows; multiplying coordinates by three is insufficient. Inspect policies/reports
for partial CDS, phase and truncation. DNA matching, interval projection and
actual translation/alignment are distinct operations.

### BLASTp query spans and two-ended links {#projection-links}

```{r example-85, eval=FALSE}
# Exact CDS DNA equality supplies evidence for these selected ungapped residues.
matching <- homologs$data |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
paired_coding <- cluster_features |>
  mutate(phase = 0)
paired_cds <- build_ggchord_cds(paired_coding)
protein_link <- tibble(
  qfeature_id = matching$qfeature_id, sfeature_id = matching$sfeature_id,
  qstart = 1, qend = 20, sstart = 1, send = 20
)
projected_links <- project_ggchord_links(protein_link, paired_cds, ungapped = TRUE)
projected_links
```


This ungapped case relies on [verified identical coding DNA](#homology).
Real BLASTp HSPs may contain gaps: query spans can still be projected, but paired
links need the subject CDS and justified ungapped correspondence. See
[real BLASTp import/projection](#alignments-protein). This version does not
reinterpret aa as bp or add native protein-coordinate plotting.

### Check your result {#projection-check-result}
Check parent CDS IDs, projection reports and returned segments. The selected residue range is a display example, not a detected domain.

## Features, stacking and genomic decoration {#annotations}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Draw real annotations as independent layers, choose suitable shapes and share stacking positions between overlapping intervals and text.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#annotations-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-86, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(

gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
feature_palette <- c(

  primer_bind = "#A020F0", misc_feature = "#A6ACB3", protein_bind = "#31849B"

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)

library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
feature_source <- find_common_features(plasmid_example_pUC19)
features <- feature_source |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
```

</details>

### Preserve feature semantics {#annotations-stack}
The preparation above loads the actual pUC19 annotations; the [circular example](#modes-circular) introduces their roles.
This table retains actual overlapping pUC19 annotations and unknown strands. Geometry and fill map separately
from the same category; an explicit fixed `shape` would override shape mapping.


```{r example-87, eval=FALSE}
stack_features <- features |>
  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
stack_position <- position_feature_stack(spacing = .12)
feature_shapes <- setNames(ifelse(names(feature_palette) == "CDS", "arrow", "block"), names(feature_palette))
p_stack <- ggchord(seq_data = plasmid_seq) +
  geom_seq(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_feature(aes(feature_fill = type, feature_shape = type),
    data = stack_features,
    width = .08, position = stack_position
  ) +
  geom_feature_label_repel(data = stack_features, position = stack_position, size = 3.8, label_fit = "shrink", label_min_size = 2.8) +
  scale_feature_shape_manual(values = feature_shapes) +
  scale_feature_fill_manual(values = feature_palette) +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis() +
  doc_theme
p_stack
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/featurestack.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/featurestack.jpg" alt="Stacked overlapping annotations from the pUC19 reference" width="1440" height="720" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Stacked overlapping annotations from the pUC19 reference · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

`position_feature_stack()` resolves overlapping annotation lanes. The label layer
uses the same Position, so text anchors follow those lanes. Prefer unique
`feature_id` values for subset/reordered label inputs. The strict gene shortcut
requires known `+/-`; general features retain unknown/bidirectional semantics.

### Choose shapes by meaning {#annotations-shapes}
| Geometry | Typical use | Important distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `arrow`, `compact_arrow` | Directional coding/feature interval | Known direction is evidence, not a display guess |
| `block`, `capped_line` | Region or unfilled interval | Shape choice does not infer biological function |
| `promoter_arrow`, `primer_arrow`, `primer_arc` | Declared promoter/primer-style annotation | Computational matching and drawing are separate |
| `marker`, `chevron`, `lollipop` | Custom interval/point-like emphasis | Keep real interval metadata; display shape is a mapping |

`geom_gene()` and `geom_feature_plasmid()` are useful presets, not aliases with
identical defaults. Use `position_strand()` for signed offsets and
`position_plasmid()` as a circular placement preset; the latter is not a fourth
coordinate mode.

### Highlight an interval without rewriting observations {#annotations-decoration}

```{r example-88, eval=FALSE}
regions <- tibble(
  accver = links$qaccver[1], start = min(links$qstart[1], links$qend[1]),
  end = max(links$qstart[1], links$qend[1]), category = "alignment interval"
)
p_decorated <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = links) +
  geom_seq_region(aes(region_fill = category), data = regions, colour = NA) +
  geom_link_ribbon(fill = "#6BAFA6", alpha = .4) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  scale_region_fill_manual(values = c("alignment interval" = "#F4D35E")) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  geom_seq_scale(length = 10000) +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis() +
  doc_theme
p_decorated
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/decorations.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/decorations.jpg" alt="Highlighting the query interval of an observed alignment" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Highlighting the query interval of an observed alignment · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

A region overlay uses its own table and `region_fill` scale. `geom_seq_label()`
names sequences, `geom_seq_center_label()` supplies name/length in a single circle,
and `geom_seq_break()` marks cropped/segmented ends. `geom_seq_scale()` is an
independent bp reference bar for collinear plots; it differs from
`scale_seq_position_continuous()`, which controls genomic axes on sequences.
An ordinary ggplot2 annotation should use [position mapping](#views-mapping)
instead of treating bp as Cartesian x/y.

### Check your result {#annotations-check-result}
Check intervals and strands before shapes and labels. Unknown strands remain in general features; stacking changes display placement, not genomic coordinates.

## Labels and local placement {#labels}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Arrange text while retaining annotation geometry: choose export dimensions and a label subset before choosing automatic or fixed placement.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#labels-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-89, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}
```

</details>

### Select a layout {#labels-layout}
Gene labels offer `"auto"`, `"radial"` and `"arc"` layouts. General feature
labels additionally support the internal-first `"feature"` default and external
`"callout"` layout. Choose the documented values for the layer you use; they are
not interchangeable presets.

After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-90, eval=FALSE}
label_data <- gene_data_example |>
  filter(anno != "hypothetical protein") |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand, anno)
p_labels <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_gene() +
  geom_gene_label_repel(data = label_data, label_layout = "auto", size = 4, label_wrap = 22) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  doc_theme
p_labels
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/labels.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/labels.jpg" alt="Automatic placement of informative source gene annotations" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Automatic placement of informative source gene annotations · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

### Fixed and automatic placement {#labels-fixed}
Use `geom_gene_label()` or `geom_feature_label()` for manual `label_rotation`,
radial/circumferential offsets and orientation controls. Automatic layers reject
these manual controls: choose `label_layout` or remove the manual argument.
Use `size`, `colour` and `family` for supported fixed text styles.

`label_fit`, `label_wrap`, `label_max_lines` and `label_min_size` control fitting
where supported. Shrinking is explicit and bounded. Unresolved labels may move
or hide; the feature geometry remains. Inspect `label_fit_diagnostics` and
`label_diagnostics` at the final export size.

### Match anchors across layers {#labels-anchors}
In collinear mode, an omitted feature-label Position inherits an unambiguous
matching feature layer. Unique `feature_id` permits reordering or subsets, but
accession, interval and strand must agree. Multiple matching layers need an
explicit Position or unambiguous IDs. Preview after selecting the final device
size; resizing the Plots pane changes the available space.

### Compare the three gene layouts {#labels-comparison}

```{r example-91, eval=FALSE}
# Compare layouts with at most the first and last informative label per sequence.
comparison_labels <- label_data |>
  group_by(accver) |>
  filter(row_number() %in% c(1L, n())) |>
  ungroup()
label_plots <- lapply(c("auto", "radial", "arc"), function(layout) {
  ggchord(seq_data = seqs, gene_data = genes) +
    geom_seq() +
    geom_gene() +
    geom_gene_label_repel(data = comparison_labels, label_layout = layout, size = 4, label_wrap = 22) +
    geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
    scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette, name = "Sequence",
      guide = guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 2, theme = doc_legend_theme)) +
    scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette, breaks = c("+", "-"), name = "Strand", guide = strand_guide) +
    coord_chord(xlim = c(-1.8, 1.8), ylim = c(-1.6, 1.6)) +
    theme_ggchord_publication(axis = element_blank()) +
    doc_legend_theme +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_blank()
    ) +
    labs(title = layout)
})
names(label_plots) <- c("auto", "radial", "arc")
p_manual_labels <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_gene() +
  geom_gene_label(data = label_data, label_rotation = 30) +
  coord_collinear()
label_plots$auto
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/labelauto.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/labelauto.jpg" alt="Informative gene annotations with automatic side placement" width="1728" height="1440" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Informative gene annotations with automatic side placement · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/labelradial.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/labelradial.jpg" alt="The same gene annotations with radial placement" width="1728" height="1440" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The same gene annotations with radial placement · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/labelarc.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/labelarc.jpg" alt="The same gene annotations with arc-oriented text" width="1728" height="1440" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The same gene annotations with arc-oriented text · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Keep at most the first and last informative labels per sequence, retaining all gene arrows, to compare text orientation.
Print `label_plots$auto`, `$radial` or `$arc` to inspect a candidate. The inputs and
requested font size are identical; only the layout choice changes. Auto uses
shared columns where applicable, radial follows local contours and arc follows
the sequence tangent. `p_manual_labels` shows the separate fixed-label route;
its explicit rotation does not belong in an automatic repel layer.
General feature labels have additional internal-first/callout choices; see the
[complete circular workflow](#plasmids) for dense mixed annotation and
[stacking](#annotations-stack) for inherited or explicit Position anchors.

### Check your result {#labels-check-result}
The three layout comparisons share the same input. Assess text direction, leaders and hiding reasons together; missing text does not mean a feature was lost.

## Quantitative tracks {#tracks}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Compute GC fractions from real DNA, then add bars, a moving mean and an annotation band. Each track has an explicit unit, window and baseline.</p></div>

### Prepare this page {#tracks-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-92, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
plasmid_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)

  select(accver, start, end, strand, type, anno)
```

</details>

### Compute a track from actual DNA {#tracks-domain}
After this page’s preparation code, compute GC fraction in 100 bp
windows of bundled pUC19. The final shorter window uses its actual base count.



```{r example-93, eval=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
data(plasmid_example_pUC19)
track_seq <- plasmid_example_pUC19 |>
  select(accver, length)
starts <- seq.int(1L, track_seq$length, by = 100L)
gc_fraction <- function(sequence) {
  bases <- strsplit(sequence, "")[[1]]
  mean(bases %in% c("G", "C"))
}
bins <- tibble(
  accver = track_seq$accver,
  start = starts,
  end = pmin(starts + 99L, track_seq$length)
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(gc = gc_fraction(substr(plasmid_example_pUC19$sequence, start, end))) |>
  ungroup()
head(bins)
```


Each row of `bins` is an actual sequence window. Check its endpoints and `gc`, then map values to track height and colour.

#### Draw GC fractions {#tracks-draw-gc}


```{r example-94, eval=FALSE}
p_tracks <- ggchord(seq_data = track_seq) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_center_label() +
  geom_track_bar(aes(track_value = gc, track_fill = gc),
    data = bins,
    position = position_track("gc", width = unit(10, "mm"))
  ) +
  scale_track_value_continuous("gc", limits = c(0, 1), unit = "GC fraction") +
  scale_track_fill_gradientn("gc", colours = c("#E4F3EA", "#65B79B", "#27775C")) +
  coord_circular() +
  doc_theme
p_tracks
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/tracks.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/tracks.jpg" alt="GC fractions computed from the bundled pUC19 DNA" width="1296" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>GC fractions computed from the bundled pUC19 DNA · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

The domain is 0–1, in fractions. Replace it with the actual unit/range of other
measurements. `position_track()` controls placement/physical width;
`scale_track_value_continuous()` controls numerical mapping.

### Share an ID deliberately {#tracks-sharing}
Same-ID layers share a numerical domain, including bar baselines, and must agree
on width/placement. Colour scales are scoped independently by track ID. Tiles
show interval categories, lines connect observations, bars encode interval values
relative to a baseline. Sharing a domain does not require sharing a spatial band.

### Inspect retention and limits {#tracks-diagnostics}
The export's `track_registry` and `track_diagnostics` record domains, physical
sizes, native offsets and clipping. Omitted/clipped rows do not mean zero values.
Focus tracks with `focus_ggchord_track()` using the same windows.

### Combine bars, a moving mean and annotation bands {#tracks-multiple}
Run the [circular example](#modes-circular) to obtain real `features` first.


```{r example-95, eval=FALSE}
line_bins <- bins |>
  transmute(
    accver,
    pos = floor((start + end) / 2),
    gc_mean = as.numeric(stats::filter(gc, rep(1 / 3, 3), sides = 2))
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(gc_mean))
categories <- features |>
  select(accver, start, end, type)
p_multitrack <- ggchord(seq_data = track_seq) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_seq_center_label() +
  geom_track_bar(aes(track_value = gc, track_fill = gc),
    data = bins,
    position = position_track("gc", width = unit(10, "mm"))
  ) +
  geom_track_line(aes(track_value = gc_mean),
    data = line_bins,
    position = position_track("gc", width = unit(10, "mm")), colour = "#233E4A"
  ) +
  scale_track_value_continuous("gc", limits = c(0, 1), unit = "GC fraction") +
  scale_track_fill_gradientn("gc", colours = c("#E4F3EA", "#65B79B", "#27775C")) +
  geom_track_tile(aes(track_fill = type),
    data = categories,
    position = position_track("features", order = 2, width = unit(2, "mm"))
  ) +
  scale_track_fill_manual("features", values = feature_palette) +
  coord_circular() +
  doc_theme +
  theme(legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left")
focused_bins <- focus_ggchord_track(bins, track_seq,
  loci = tibble(accver = track_seq$accver, start = 500, end = 1500), type = "interval"
)
p_multitrack
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/multitrack.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/multitrack.jpg" alt="pUC19 GC fractions, a three-bin moving mean and annotation bands" width="1296" height="1152" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>pUC19 GC fractions, a three-bin moving mean and annotation bands · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

Bars and line use the same actual GC measurements; the line is a three-window
moving mean. Incomplete end windows are omitted, not filled with invented values.
Line positions use integer bin midpoints. Annotation bands have an independent ID
and palette. Bands are explicitly ordered outside; overly wide inner bands at
small radii can fold and are rejected.

### Check your result {#tracks-check-result}
GC in bins lies between 0 and 1; each row is an actual window and the last may be shorter than 100 bp. Continuous colour expresses values; the category band expresses feature types, not GC magnitude.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#output">Export, preview and diagnostics →</a></div>

### Save this result {#tracks-save-result}
Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

```{r example-96, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("pUC19-tracks.png", p_multitrack, width = 9, height = 8, units = "in", dpi = 144)
```

### Prepare this page {#styling-prepare}

</details>

### Build styles from data roles {#styling-roles}
The preparation above declares the inputs and shared appearance. The example declares categories
explicitly: ribbon fill maps query ID; sequence colour maps sequence ID; gene fill
maps strand. Manual scale names match those values exactly.


```{r example-98, eval=FALSE}
p_styled <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = links, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = qaccver), alpha = .5) +
  geom_gene() +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  coord_collinear() +
  doc_axis() +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  guides(gene_fill = guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)) +
  doc_theme
theme_variants <- list(minimal = theme_ggchord_minimal(), dark = theme_ggchord_dark(), plasmid = theme_ggchord_plasmid())
p_styled
```

<figure class="documentation-figure"><a class="figure-link" href="tutorial-assets/styling.jpg" title="Click to enlarge"><img data-external="1" src="tutorial-assets/styling.jpg" alt="Explicit sequence, strand and query-category colour scales" width="1440" height="864" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>Explicit sequence, strand and query-category colour scales · <span class="figure-hint">Click to enlarge</span></figcaption></figure>

| Role | Mapped data | Useful scale family |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `seq_colour`, `seq_ring` | Sequence/category | Sequence colour or ring manual scales |
| `ribbon_fill`, `ribbon_alpha`, `ribbon_colour`, `ribbon_linetype` | Alignment metadata or statistics | Manual, gradient/steps/identity and alpha scales |
| `feature_fill`, `feature_shape`, `gene_fill`, `region_fill` | Annotation category or strand | Role-specific manual/preset scales |
| `link_colour`, `link_alpha`, `link_linewidth`, `link_linetype` | Point-link metadata | Continuous or manual link scales |
| `track_value`, `track_fill`, `track_colour` | Values/categories in one named track | Named value domain and colour/fill scales |

### Fixed styles and user scale priority {#styling-priority}
Put a constant style outside `aes()`. Map variable styles inside it and supply an
appropriate scale. An explicitly fixed geom value takes precedence; omitting that
argument keeps mapping active. Your scale takes priority over automatic defaults.
Repeated same-kind layers keep independent data/mapping/parameters. A geometric
vector named by `accver` does not mean a scale also accepts per-sequence lists.

### Make legends readable {#styling-guides}
`guide_ggchord_legend()` controls discrete role legends; `guide_ggchord_colourbar()`
controls continuous colour guides. The colour/color spelling aliases are retained,
with `colour` preferred in this documentation. Use `show.legend` on a layer,
`guides()` for guide choices and `theme(legend.position = ...)` for placement.
A wide guide may need multiple rows or a wider export, not smaller biological data.

### Select a theme for the scene {#styling-themes}
The example stores minimal, dark and plasmid alternatives in `theme_variants`.
Add the appropriate object to the matching plot. `theme_ggchord_publication()`
is used above; the plasmid preset belongs with the circular workflow. These
objects style non-data appearance. They do not choose a coordinate system or
replace data-driven fill scales. Use `theme(text = element_text(...))` for text
appearance; removed `base_size` constructor-style shortcuts have a
[migration route](#migration).

### Check your result {#styling-check-result}
Links from the same query share a colour; continuous identity needs a continuous scale. Put fixed colours outside aes() and make each guide explain its mapping.

<div class="next-step">Continue: <a href="#adjustments">Common adjustments and grammar →</a></div>


## Set values by sequence and strand {#parameters}

<div class="task-intro"><p>Adjust geometry by sequence or strand, retaining useful flexible parameter formats while making their scope explicit.</p></div>

Previously described as “flexible parameter formats”, this feature configures geometry per sequence or strand.

### Prepare this page {#parameters-prepare}
In a fresh R session, run the code below, then follow this page in order. Colours and layout are optional display choices; inputs select only the fields needed.

<details class="preparation"><summary>Preparation code — run once on this page</summary>

```{r example-99, eval=FALSE}
library(ggchord)
library(dplyr)
data(seq_data_example)
data(ribbon_data_example)
data(gene_data_example)
seqs <- seq_data_example |>
  select(accver, length)
links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send)
# The fixture preserves biological strands separately from its old display strands.
genes <- gene_data_example |>
  transmute(accver, start, end, strand = source_strand)

# Optional appearance choices; none of these columns or scales is required input.
library(ggchord)
seq_palette <- setNames(
  c("#E64B35", "#233E4A", "#269B82", "#D59B17"),
  c("MT108731.1", "MT118296.1", "OQ646790.1", "OR222515.1")
)
gene_palette <- c("+" = "#CE1536", "-" = "#346B9D", "." = "#8291A6")

library(ggchord)
doc_background <- "#FFFCF5"
identity_palette <- c("#303B71", "#36537D", "#269B82", "#A5D52C", "#ECEB31")
identity_values <- c(0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9, 1)
identity_breaks <- c(0, 50, 80, 90, 100)
doc_legend_theme <- theme(
  legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
  legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
  legend.margin = margin(l = 4, r = 4, unit = "mm")
)
sequence_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(nrow = 1, theme = doc_legend_theme)
strand_guide <- guide_ggchord_legend(
  nrow = 1, override.aes = list(strand = c("+", "-")), theme = doc_legend_theme
)
identity_guide <- guide_ggchord_colourbar(
  position = "left", direction = "vertical",
  theme = theme(
    legend.key.height = unit(75, "mm"), legend.key.width = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11), legend.margin = margin(r = 7, unit = "mm")
  )
)
doc_theme <- theme_ggchord_publication(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
  axis.text.check.overlap = TRUE
) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.key.width = unit(9, "mm"), legend.key.height = unit(5, "mm"),
    legend.spacing.x = unit(9, "mm"), legend.spacing.y = unit(7, "mm"),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "mm"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = doc_background, colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#5C625A"),
    plot.margin = margin(14, 18, 14, 18)
  )
doc_axis <- function(coordinates = "relative") {
  scale_seq_position_continuous(
    coordinates = coordinates, n.breaks = 3, minor_breaks = NULL,
    labels = function(x) format(x, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
  )
}
```

</details>

### The capability remains supported {#parameters-recommendation}
Sequence-local geometry often needs one value per sequence or strand; duplicating
whole layers would obscure that intent. Keep scalars as the default, use vectors
named by `accver` when values differ, and name strand pairs `+`/`-`.


```{r example-100, eval=FALSE}
# Sequence IDs remain stable when the data is reordered; positional lists do not.
radii <- setNames(c(1.1, 1, 1, 1), seqs$accver)
widths <- c("+" = .045, "-" = .065)
p_parameters <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, gene_data = genes) +
  geom_seq(seq_radius = radii) +
  geom_gene(
    width = widths,
    position = position_strand(c("+" = .08, "-" = -.1))
  ) +
  geom_seq_label(size = 4) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  scale_gene_fill_manual(values = gene_palette) +
  coord_chord() +
  doc_theme
p_parameters
```


Run this page’s preparation code first. Named radii survive sequence
reordering; unnamed entries follow current positions. These are layout/geometry
values, not a universal extension to colours or themes.

### Supported parameters {#parameters-scope}
| Interface | Parameters | Matching scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `geom_seq()` | `seq_radius`, `seq_curvature`, `seq_gap`, `seq_orientation` | Sequence; radius/curvature effects depend on coordinates |
| `geom_seq_label()` | `labels`, `seq_label_radius`, `seq_label_rotation`, `size`, `seq_label_hjust`, `seq_label_vjust` | Sequence; `seq_label_orientation` is one mode choice |
| `geom_link_ribbon()` / `geom_link_line()` | `link_gap` | Endpoint sequence; Cartesian control points are not per-sequence scalars |
| `geom_gene()` / `geom_feature()` | `width` | Sequence and/or `+`/`-` strand |
| `position_strand()` / `position_plasmid()` | `offset` | Sequence/strand; prefer Positions over compatibility offset inputs |
| Fixed `geom_gene_label()` / `geom_feature_label()` | `label_radial_offset`, `label_circum_offset`, `label_circum_limit`, `label_rotation` | Sequence/strand, not every text setting |
| `position_track()` | Numeric `width`, `gap` | Native numeric placement by sequence; physical `unit()` is a scalar absolute size |

`seq_order` is itself an ordering. Automatic `label_layout` is a mode; manual angles
and offsets belong to fixed label layers rather than automatic-label `...`.
Axes/themes, aesthetics, scales and guides do not inherit the list extension.
Manual scales do accept vectors named by **data categories**, under ordinary
ggplot2 scale semantics; see [styling](#styling).

### Compatibility and design tradeoffs {#parameters-compatibility}
Equal-length unnamed vectors, sequence-named lists, position-named lists and
unnamed lists remain compatible. Gene/feature entries can additionally contain
strand pairs. Each parameter still validates its own type, length, range and units.
This does not make a list a valid container for any argument.

The v0.16.6 RC audit retains these equivalent forms: no deletion or deprecation
is announced. Positional forms follow the current displayed sequence order after
filtering; names take precedence when they match accession IDs. In width/fixed-label
lists, a per-sequence entry is a strand pair; `list(value)` is the scalar recycling
form. Position offsets also accept scalar entries per sequence. Explicit
strand-named Position offsets are signed; an omitted strand or sequence uses zero.
`position_plasmid()` uses one shared offset and rejects strand pairs.
Use unique keys: accession IDs `"1"`, `"+"` or `"-"` can be ambiguous with index/strand
shorthand, so prefer sequence-named nested lists for strand values. Native track
width/gap must cover all displayed sequences. These rules do not extend to themes.

Numeric values do not all share one unit: `seq_gap` is a proportion, rotations
are degrees, and physical track sizes use explicit `unit()` values. `seq_backbone_gap`
and `seq_backbone_width` are scalar style controls, not members of the list rule.
Automatic collinear orientation belongs to `coord_collinear(orientation = "auto")`;
`geom_seq(seq_orientation = ...)` supplies numerical +1/-1 sequence directions.

### Check your result {#parameters-check-result}
Named-vector keys must match actual accver values or +/− strands. Recheck matching after reordering; list rules do not extend to themes, scales or aesthetics.

### Assign each responsibility {#adjustments-grammar}
| Task | Interface |
| --- | --- |
| Map a column to an aesthetic | `aes()` |
| Define mapping and guide | `scale_*()`, `guides()` |
| Geometry and fixed style | `geom_*()` |
| Local placement | `position_*()` |
| Global coordinate system | `coord_*()` |
| Non-data appearance | `theme_*()`, `theme()` |
| Titles and captions | `labs()` |

Fixed styles may be supplied directly to geoms. Data-driven variation needs a
mapping and scale. An explicit fixed value overrides its mapping; omitting the
fixed argument preserves the mapping. User scales override inferred defaults.
`shape` is the fixed feature geometry parameter; `feature_shape` remains the
mapped role. Explicit `shape = NULL` is invalid, not a request to use a mapping.

### Map link identity {#adjustments-mapping}
After this page’s preparation code:


```{r example-102, eval=FALSE}
identity_links <- ribbon_data_example |>
  select(qaccver, saccver, qstart, qend, sstart, send, pident)
p_mapped <- ggchord(seq_data = seqs, ribbon_data = identity_links) +
  geom_seq() +
  geom_link_ribbon(aes(ribbon_fill = pident), alpha = .6) +
  scale_ribbon_fill_gradientn(
    colours = identity_palette, values = identity_values,
    limits = c(0, 100), breaks = identity_breaks, name = "Identity (%)", guide = identity_guide
  ) +
  scale_seq_colour_manual(values = seq_palette) +
  coord_chord(rotation = 20) +
  labs(title = "Sequence comparison") +
  doc_theme
p_mapped
```


### Place features {#adjustments-position}
Use `position_strand(c("+" = .1, "-" = -.2))` for signed strand offsets.
`position_feature_stack()` handles overlapping features; `position_track()`
allocates a named quantitative lane. Geometric sequence parameters accept one
value, a matching unnamed vector, or a vector named by `accver`; named vectors
are recommended. This syntax does not extend to scales, guides or themes.

Each layer owns its own `data`, `mapping` and parameters. Repeated feature or
link layers do not replace one another. Use ordinary ggplot2 `show.legend` and
`inherit.aes`; role input mappings precede geometry, while staged visual mappings
follow ggplot2 evaluation. See the API contract (`help("ggchord_api_contract", package = "ggchord")`).

### Check your result {#adjustments-check-result}
Use a coordinate for global rotation, named values for per-sequence geometry, and mappings plus scales for data-dependent colour.
